# Neat Racing Voxel Racer (neatRacing)

**Status:** [WIP]

<!-- Derived from plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.spec.md (spec sections 13, 17, 18, 12.4-12.5).
     This is the tracker for the neatRacing voxel racer flagship demo. Phase/step/slice
     structure mirrors spec section 17 phases P1/P2/P3 1:1 with slice_ids kept verbatim
     so section 18 traceability holds without renumbering. Planning-only authoring pass:
     no src/, docs/, examples/, or scripts/ production edits. -->

## Scope

- Implement the neatRacing voxel racer per `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.spec.md`:
  Phase 1 graphics engine + manual keyboard driving (AC-001..AC-024 + AC-040..AC-042),
  Phase 2 AI migration with NGE growth engine (AC-025..AC-034 + AC-043),
  Phase 3 polish + deprecation prep (AC-035..AC-039).
- Planning-only pass in this instance: author full machine-readable step packets,
  register the plan, rebind the session, reindex RAG, prove gates. Execution is
  dispatched step-by-step to implementing/testing specialists after verification.
- Single source of truth for acceptance criteria and validation commands is the spec
  (section 13 ACs, section 12.5 conventions); this tracker binds each spec slice to its
  ACs, files, red-test notes, and validation commands.

## Mandates

- **Planning-only:** this authoring pass edits only `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md`,
  `plans/README.md`, `plans/Roadmap.md`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, and RAG index artifacts.
- **Spec lock:** spec section 12 locked decisions register (LD) and resolved open
  questions are not reopened by the tracker. Deprecation prep is notices-only
  (LD-33); removal of `examples/racing_curriculum` is a separate user-confirmed
  workstream and out of scope.
- **Machine-readable packets:** every execution step carries a YAML packet with
  `expansion: slices`, `auto_expand: true`, and a `tdd_sequence` that MATCHES the
  slice roles the packet carries (`red-green` when the FIRST slice is a
  red-testing slice, `green-only` when the first slice is an implementing slice),
  and typed slices (slice_id / title / status / goal / estimate_hours /
  files_to_change / acceptance_criteria / parallelizable / dependencies) per the
  step-packet gate schema.
- **Slice discipline:** each slice is one atomic behavioral intent bound to spec
  section 17; at most 3 code files per slice (sibling `*.test.ts` files count;
  trivial one-line config registrations such as a package.json script line or a
  tsconfig include may accompany without counting); estimate_hours <= 4; at most
  5 slices per step - a step that needs a SIXTH slice is SPLIT into two steps
  and the split is recorded in the wave note, in the phase step list and in the
  plan tail (the at-most-5 limit is a MANDATE: a deviation is never recorded in
  its place, and a split NEVER defers a re-pin away from the production change
  that invalidated the pin).
- **Red-first:** every implementation slice carries `red_test` notes (the failing
  assertion to author first) honoring the spec RED -> IMPLEMENT -> GREEN rule; each
  step ends with a green-testing slice that runs the section 12.5 validation list.
- **Named constants:** tuning values use the named constants from the spec open
  questions patch (NEATRACING_FIXED_RENDER_HEIGHT, NEATRACING_MAX_BACKING_WIDTH,
  NEATRACING_AI_MIN_SESSION_LAPS, NEATRACING_EDITOR_UNDO_BUDGET_BYTES,
  NEATRACING_REBUILD_P95_BUDGET_MS, NEATRACING_ADAPTATION_TICK_BUDGET_MS, etc.).
- **Zero per-frame allocation (P9)** and **capacity limits preserved** (maxNodes 8000 /
  maxConnections 32000, AC-029) are standing constraints on all Phase 1/2 slices.
- **No deferred cleanup:** when a slice replaces an existing module or script, the old
  code is removed in the same slice.
- **No git:** agents never run git commands; all changes land via direct file edits.
- **Evidence:** gate runs are recorded in `## Latest validation evidence`; green-light
  recording is reserved for the separate verification instance.

### AC-087..AC-090 RE-DERIVATION (2026-10-27, verdict-4 + verdict-5, 01-planning AUTHOR)

**Scope of this subsection.** The author_handoff item 5 of the `verdict5-merged-gap-map` record: *keep AC-087..AC-090 semantics and re-derive their numeric pins from the equilibrium + the manual-mode rule*. The four SEMANTICS are unchanged (slide prominence with a recorded feel direction, a measurable traction signal, a no-regression ledger, and a user visual gate). The NUMERIC PINS are re-derived, because every pin that was written against the pre-wave model, against the AI-mode page, or against a transient reading is either vacuous or unreachable after the re-wiring. This subsection is the single home of the re-derivation; the row text above only points here.

**The two rules that drive every re-derived pin (the merged-map `acceptance_rules_for_the_author`):**

- **R-MANUAL (the measurement lane):** every slide, camera and traction measurement is taken with the page in **MANUAL** mode and the car **ON THE ROAD**. The ai-mode page is never acceptable evidence (R-M3). The page used to boot in AI mode (`INITIAL_RACE_MODE = MODE_OPTION_AI`, `examples/neatRacing/host/mode-selector.ts:63`), and the autopilot only crosses the `|steer| >= 0.5` engage cliff on **176 of 7200 ticks (2.44 %)** — so the AI page barely ever produces the slide the user is judging. The off-road excursion is the second mask: the demo track puts the car **OFF-ROAD at tick 280 at 82.3 m/s** (921 of 1200 ticks), where the `22.25 m/s` floor pins the car at `80.1 km/h` and the off-road deceleration is **32 : 1** the drift scrub — the slide is arithmetically erased. The re-wiring therefore starts with the two masks: the boot mode (Step 14P, slice `P1-drift-rewire-boot-mode`) and a ROAD-ONLY surface classification (Step 14P, slice `P1-drift-rewire-road-surface`).
- **R-EQUILIBRIUM (the deficit pin):** the speed deficit is pinned at the **EQUILIBRIUM 32.911 km/h** (the envelope audit), **never** at a transient 600-tick reading (which reads `32.555 km/h`). The repeat-offence in this plan has been to pin a transient; the re-derived contract waits for a convergence criterion and then measures.

**AC-087 (slide prominence) — semantics retained, pins re-derived.** The semantics are retained exactly: a **named** slide-prominence floor; the feel **direction decided and recorded in this plan before any production edit** (a bigger slide — decision D-11); the user-approved body-animation **shape** retained (the second-order pose spring with the steer-articulation term); and a sustained-slide contract. The re-derived pins:

1. The floor stays asserted on the **deterministic unit proxy** (`computeDriftSlideProxyRad(slipAngleRad)`), and the browser reading stays a loose **presence** observable (`driftFeelSlideProminence`) that is never numerically compared against a constant. (Unchanged — this pin was already correct.)
2. **The slide DEPTH becomes SPEED-PROPORTIONAL.** The measured defect is that the committed slide is the **same 0.45 rad at 5 m/s and at 89 m/s** (the envelope audit): the entry ramp is a fixed `3.5 rad/s` (speed-independent) and the clamp is reached in 8 ticks at every speed. The re-derived contract: the depth at the top speed is at least `0.45 rad` **and** the depth at a low speed is at most `0.20 rad` (the exact split is a RED decision, `P1-drift-law-red` / RED-2). This is the physics half of the user's "the tires should lose traction also proportionally to the speed".
3. The **sustained-slide window** is measured **on the road, in MANUAL mode** (the off-road lane pins the car at 80.1 km/h and masks the slide).
4. The **speed deficit** is pinned at the **equilibrium 32.911 km/h**, never at the transient.
5. The camera and the body read the **same published slip** (the one shared scalar), so the frame can never be internally inconsistent — a travel-locked camera with a crabbing body is the exact defect the audits forbid. The camera aim is the **travel heading published on the physics state** (the new named field `travelHeadingRad`), and the body yaw source is switched from the **committed** slip to the **published** slip (the call site `examples/neatRacing/physics/physics.step.service.ts:457`).
6. **The 3D VIEW must MOVE.** A new red contract (`P1-drift-rewire-red` / RED-4, and the W4b contract A12) asserts the **camera basis** — the look target and the forward vector — differs from the nose-aligned values by the travel divergence, and is **bit-identical to the pre-wave basis** when the published slip is zero. The assertion never targets the seam or a channel value: the A1–A11 contracts and all 43 fixture checks can pass with a **frozen** camera, which is the trap the F3 finding names.

**AC-088 (traction) — semantics retained, substance corrected.** The semantics are retained: the tire traction loss is a **measurable, non-degenerate** contract rather than a feel claim. The substance is corrected, because the old contract measured two things that are not traction at all:

| Old measured quantity | Why it is not a traction signal | Re-derived quantity |
|---|---|---|
| a **fixed-sun lighting band** (the tire gradient, G-V4) | it is a lighting term, not a friction term | the per-tire grip and the tire gradient are driven by the **published traction severity** |
| the **raw steer echo** (the front-wheel yaw, G-V5) | it echoes the input, not the physics | the front-wheel yaw is driven by the **physics state** |
| the **committed slip** (the crab, G-V3) | the traction law reads the **published** slip, so the two disagree | **one** shared scalar, published on the state as `tractionSeverity` |

The re-derived contract: the severity is a **named function of the speed and the published slip** (the user law S-2/S-3), published on the state, `0` on a straight line, `1` at the full slide, **monotonic** in the slide depth, and computed on the **post-traction `car.speed`** — the same basis the traction law uses (the F11 rule: the basis must match, or the camera and the tires disagree). **No consumer re-derives it**: the car pass, the HUD, the camera and the debug seam all read the same field.

**AC-089 (no regression) — preserve set retained, re-baselined set extended.** The **PRESERVE SET** is unchanged and is never relaxed: AC-047A..AC-047D (the AC-047D byte-identity is re-anchored on the **production serializer** — a stronger contract than the whole-object `JSON.stringify` pin), the determinism twin-runs, the straight-line exact zeros, the low-speed exact-zero gate, AC-078 and its tyre-follow tolerance, and the 24 non-drift fixture checks. The **RE-BASELINED SET** gains, each with exactly **one ledger row** whose single home is **this plan** (the pin, the old baseline, the new baseline, the **measured** value, the owner file):

| Pin | Invalidated by | Owner slice | Home |

| the physics state shape (the new `travelHeadingRad` and `tractionSeverity` fields) | the state contract change | `P1-drift-rewire-travel-camera`, `P1-drift-traction-scalar` | the ledger in this plan |
| the **DECLARED POSE ENVELOPE** (re-derived from the **published** slip ceiling, so the `0.002 rad` published overshoot can never breach it) | the body-yaw source change + the re-derived gain | `P1-drift-rewire-travel-camera` (source), `P1-drift-law-proportional` (the gain and the envelope) | the ledger in this plan |
| the body yaw gain `NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD` (the `0.5` cosmetic gain; the RED-decided value is **`0.45`** — RE-PINNED 2026-10-27 by the 01-planning PATCH from the INFEASIBLE `0.75` recommendation: the anti-null guard `|GAIN - 1| >= 0.5` caps GAIN at 0.5, the 0.2 rad prominence floor against the 0.45 rad max slip forces `GAIN >= 0.4444` below 1, and the pose settle band [30, 34] ticks needs `GAIN >= ~0.386`, so the FEASIBLE WINDOW is [0.386, 0.5] and 0.45 is chosen inside it — the guard still passes at `|0.45 - 1| = 0.55 >= 0.5`; a slight animation, never a full tilt) | the proportional law | `P1-drift-law-proportional` (the production gain) + `P1-drift-law-repin` (the FIVE gain-coupled TEST literals) | the ledger in this plan |

**AC-090 (the user visual gate) — the verdict is REJECT and the gate is OPEN.** The **semantics** of AC-090 are retained in full: the automated contracts are necessary but not sufficient (a FEEL verdict needs a human), the gate asks the **six verbatim questions** transcribed from `plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.14N-fixture-gate.md` section 5.3, the verdict is recorded on **three surfaces** (this plan, `plans/README.md`, `plans/Roadmap.md`), the verdict is bound to the **identified bundle** (byte length + sha256), and a **REJECT re-opens** the step instead of closing it. The **re-derived** part is the state of the gate itself:

- **VERDICT 2026-10-27 = REJECT** (verdicts 4 and 5). The step is **NOT** closed, the step stays `[WIP]`, and the six questions are **RE-ASKED** against the re-wired build, in **MANUAL** mode, on the **ROAD**.
- The earlier `fix-packet-P1-drift-feel-green-iteration-4` close-out was scoped to the **HARNESS** (the fixture's own instrumentation — the one-line `resetFrameCapture()` per-frame call) and was **NEVER an AC-090 pass**. It must not be read as one, in this plan or in `plans/README.md` or `plans/Roadmap.md`.
- The deterministic verdict rule is **unchanged** (ACCEPT iff Q2 == CRISP and Q3 == CATCHES and Q4 == NO and Q5 == YES and Q6 == YES and Q1 in {YES, TOO MUCH}, with the envelope check green when Q1 == TOO MUCH; a REJECT follows on a Q2/Q3/Q6 failure, on Q1 == NO, or on Q5 == NO).
- **Who may record the verdict:** the **user**, or a fresh verification instance that is **explicitly authorised** to record the user verdict. An implementation slice and a green-testing slice **may not** record an AC-090 pass — that is a plan violation, and the Step 14R green slice carries this prohibition explicitly.

### Derivation notes

1. **1:1 slice preservation:** spec section 17 slice_ids (P1-S1-A .. P3-S2-C) appear
   verbatim with their spec file lists and AC bindings; section 18 traceability holds
   without renumbering. The tracker adds one trailing green-testing slice per execution
   step (id `<spec-step>-green`, e.g. `P1-S1-green`) to host the section 12.5
   validation sweep; spec impl slices keep goal `implementing`.
2. **a/b step splits:** spec steps with 5 impl slices (P1-S3, P1-S4, P1-S6, P1-S7,
   P2-S3) are split into part 1 (A-C) and part 2 (D-E) sub-steps because a
   gate-conformant green-only step needs at least 2 and at most 5 slices and a
   trailing green-testing slice (5 impl + 1 green = 6 > 5). Spec slice_ids, file
   lists, and AC bindings are unchanged by the split.
3. **Uniform green-only tdd_sequence:** spec slices are RED -> IMPLEMENT -> GREEN
   atomic units; per-slice RED notes live in the slice `red_test` field so the
   gate-conformant step shape is uniformly `green-only` (all-but-last slices
   `implementing`, last slice `green-testing`).
4. **Planning ACs** use the AC-PLN-001..AC-PLN-005 prefix to avoid collision with the
   spec AC-001..AC-043 numbering.
5. **Dual-parser layout contract:** two parsers coexist and this tracker satisfies both.
   The step-packet GATE parses only the fenced YAML packets (heading-agnostic). The
   neataptic-workflow MCP additionally parses HEADINGS scoped to `## Implementation
phases`: `### Phase <N> — <Title> [STATUS]` (H3 + em-dash, terminated by a
   `## …validation gates…` H2) and `#### Step <N> — <Title> [STATUS]` (H4) inside the
   phase body; the active [WIP] step also carries `**Step objective:**` and
   `**Required validation:**` prose sections (backtick commands prefix-matching the
   YAML `validation` list). Keep this shape on every future step flip.
6. **Global step numbering:** the coverage backlog `Step` column uses global
   step numbers across phases — Phase 1 = 02-15 (Step 13 = P1-boot-glue
   wiring; Step 14 = browser composition, inserted between Step 13 and the
   exit check per the batch-102 integration-gap classification; Step 15 =
   editor editing-loop composition, inserted between Step 14 and the exit
   check per the batch-105 editing-loop scope correction, patch #2),
   Phase 2 = 16-20, Phase 3 = 21-22. Phase 2/3 rows were renumbered from
   the pre-insertion global sequence (batch 19 item 78 obs a), re-renumbered
   after the batch-102 Step 14 insertion, and re-renumbered again after the
   batch-105 Step 15 insertion (the batch-26 renumber precedent) so
   "13"/"14"/"15" bind uniquely to Phase 1 steps and Phase 2 starts at
   global 16.

The magnitude is deliberately NOT pinned to a single value: the effect is binary, so any value >= 1e-12 m recovers the full budget - but the constant MUST be named and the AC MUST state the effective 1 m clearance so it cannot be silently relaxed. SHORTFALL ENVELOPE (measured, 8 fixture seeds x every bleacher, front row of every level): the nominal 1 m cell spacing computes to 0.99999999999997014 .. 1.0000000000000195 m depending on the bleacher orientation and the seed, i.e. a worst-case shortfall of 2.99e-14 m and a worst-case overshoot of 1.95e-14 m; at the default fixture (seed 42, the accidental host bleacher[0]) the six front-row gaps per level are 4x 0.99999999999999001 (below 1) and 2x 1.00000000000001887 (at or above 1). The margin value MUST therefore exceed 3e-14 m; the 1e-12 m floor quoted above satisfies that with ~30x headroom and is a planning judgement, not a measured optimum.'

The user reviewed the served green build after the Step 14K closure and wrote "looking great" (anchor user-bug-report-2026-10-23-sprite-scale, recorded as the 14K USER VISUAL GATE). The 20 populated bleachers, the 4 evenly spread sprites per bleacher level and the restored off-bleacher agents are accepted. The same review raised the NEXT defect - the crowd sprites look GIANT-SIZED - which is planified as Step 14L (AC-077).

**User instruction:** "use 4 sprites per bleacher level instead of 5. And evenly distributed across the whole length of the platform, it looks too crowded now" (CROWD-1); "add more bleachers, 20 in total on the track all with agents" (CROWD-2); "there are no agents outside the bleachers, there should, what happened with the mechanics? and more sprites who are not on a bleacher, and may be walking around" (CROWD-3). The report is the anchor user-bug-report-2026-10-22 at the end of this plan.

**Step objective:** Re-populate the right world the way the 2026-10-22 live-page review asks: 4 sprites per bleacher level spread evenly over the full platform length (AC-072), exactly 20 bleachers on the track with every one of them populated (AC-073), and agents outside the bleachers again - team-colored mechanics on the inner ring that look at the car, slow walkers, and standing spectators outside the ring (AC-074) - all inside the gl.MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE atlas bound (AC-075), and the per-frame billboard budget large enough that no populated bleacher is truncated away (AC-076). The retired single-host crowd, the deleted mechanic/crew path, and the closed walker seam are re-authored here; this is a reversal, never a git checkout (mutating git is BANNED).

**Decision set (2026-10-22 planning amendment):**

- **D1 - placement:** Step 14K is inserted between Step 14J and Step 14G, so the document order equals the routing-chain order 14F -> 14J -> 14K -> 14G -> 14H -> 14I -> 14E -> Step 15. The anchor asks for the step "inserted before Step 14E" and "ahead of Step 14G"; inserting it directly before 14E (after 14I) would put the document order out of chain order, so the 14J precedent is followed (the 2026-10-16 report inserted its new steps at the head of the chain, between 14F and 14G). Step 14E stays the last audited step and its audit scope now includes 14K; Step 15 keeps 14K as a prerequisite.
- **D2 - the single active boundary:** Phase 1 may hold only ONE [WIP] step (mcp-plan-utils.mjs loadActivePlanContext). The anchor calls 14K a "[PLANNED] Step" but also makes it the ACTIVE boundary ahead of 14G, so 14K is opened as [WIP] and Step 14G is DEMOTED to [PLANNED] (the 14I demotion pattern). No 14G work is lost: all its slices are DONE automated-green and only the user drift-feel / body-yaw visual verdict stays open, re-queued after 14K.
- **D3 - marker repair:** the 14G heading marker "[WIP: automated-green; drift-feel/body-yaw visual verdict pending]" is not a valid status token for the STEP_PATTERN, so the workflow binding resolved NO active step (get_active_workflow_snapshot returned activeStep: null and get_slice_context returned notFound for the 14G slice). The demotion to a clean [PLANNED] marker plus the 14K [WIP] marker repair that binding. The 14J YAML status is normalized from [WIP] to [DONE] so a closed step no longer presents itself as an active WIP block.
- **D4 - AC supersessions:** AC-072 supersedes the AC-069 row-content and level-interleaved clauses; AC-073 supersedes the AC-070 single-host clause; AC-074 supersedes the AC-070 no-people clauses; AC-075 supersedes the AC-071 public-only scope clause while retaining the BOUND. The retained clarifications (camera-relative facing, one sprite row per level with all 3 levels populated, the atlas bound, the named personal-space margin) stay invariants.
- **D5 - re-authoring, not a checkout:** the mechanic/crew module and its test were atomically deleted by P1-crowd-retire-people and mutating git is BANNED, so the off-bleacher agents are RE-AUTHORED from the logged contracts in the plan evidence and .logs.md: the public-only 144-frame atlas (6 accents x 8 directions x 3 poses) is reused, the mechanics are team-colored stand frames that look at the car, and no new atlas block is added (which keeps the retained public-only invariant and the atlas pack unchanged).
- **D6 - acceptance-criteria format:** the step-level and slice-level acceptance_criteria of 14K use the workflow-native object form (id + text) instead of the flat string form, because normalizeTestContracts (customization-utils.mjs) reads criterion.text / criterion.id and a plain string list item parses to an object with EMPTY text, which rendered the dispatched slice context with blank contract bullets. The gates accept both shapes; the object form is the only one that survives into the dispatched agent payload.
- **D7 - independent Tier-3 validation round:** a fresh read-only slice-validator instance (dispatched by this author instance, not the author itself) reviewed the 14K packet and returned PASS with four non-blocking observations, all of which are folded into this packet: (a) OBS-1 the AC-071 backlog marker now reads SUPERSEDED IN PART by AC-075 with the BOUND explicitly RETAINED; (b) OBS-2 the AC-073 backlog row now also binds P1-crowd2-seat-density and public.sprite.ts, because the per-bleacher population is implemented there; (c) OBS-3 the unowned per-frame billboard cap became a NEW AC-076 owned by P1-crowd2-off-bleacher-people (the retired shared cap MAX_BILLBOARDS = NEATRACING_DECORATION_LOD_BUDGET = 128 sized the single-host crowd and would truncate 20 x 12 = 240 seated billboards plus the off-bleacher agents, so the billboard budget becomes its own NAMED constant while the prop LOD budget keeps governing the voxel props) with the RED-F contract and the GREEN-07 measurement clause; (d) OBS-4 the now-unused getBleacherHostingFootprintArea import is named in the AC-074 (no deferred cleanup) clause of the same slice. OBS-5 (a stale NEXT BOUNDARY bullet for Step 14I inside the Latest validation evidence section) is annotated as superseded by the 14K boundary. **User instruction:** "crowd sprites look giant-sized; reduce sprite height to 1/2 current on right-world crowd billboards" (SPRITE-1). The report is the anchor user-bug-report-2026-10-23-sprite-scale at the end of this plan, raised during the same live-page review that PASSED the Step 14K user visual gate ("looking great").

**Step objective:** Halve the world size of the right-world crowd billboards so the spectators stop reading as giant-sized next to the car. The rendered world HEIGHT of every crowd billboard - the seated spectators, the team-colored inner-ring mechanics, the slow walkers and the standing off-bleacher spectators - becomes EXACTLY 1/2 of its pre-14L height, with the world WIDTH following the SAME factor so the square 192x192 px atlas frames keep their aspect ratio. The factor is ONE named exported constant, NEATRACING_PUBLIC_BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 0.5 in examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.ts, applied inside computeBillboardScale so the placement footprint and the rendered quad can never disagree; the meters-per-sprite-pixel constant stays 0.05 m/px, so a 192 px frame goes from 9.6 m tall to 4.8 m. The halving changes the GEOMETRY only: the crowd counts, the per-frame billboard budget, the camera-relative facing, the 1 m personal space and the atlas bound all stay exactly as they are (AC-077).

**Decision set (2026-10-23 planning amendment):**

- **D1 - placement:** Step 14L is inserted between Step 14K and Step 14G, so the document order equals the routing-chain order 14F -> 14J -> 14K -> 14L -> 14G -> 14H -> 14I -> 14E -> Step 15. The anchor asks for the step "inserted before Step 14E" and "ahead of Step 14G"; the 14K precedent (D1 of the 14K decision set) is followed - the new step is placed at the HEAD of the still-open chain, immediately before 14G, so the 14L/14G demotion-and-requeue pair is one adjacent swap. Step 14E stays the last audited step and its audit scope now includes 14L; Step 15 keeps 14L as a prerequisite.
- **D2 - the single active boundary:** Phase 1 may hold only ONE [WIP] step (mcp-plan-utils.mjs loadActivePlanContext). The anchor makes 14L the new active boundary, so 14L is opened as [WIP] and Step 14G is DEMOTED to [PLANNED] (the 14K demotion pattern). No 14G work is lost: all its slices are DONE automated-green and only the user drift-feel / body-yaw visual verdict plus fix-packet-P1-turn-drift-green-iteration-11 stay open, re-queued after 14L.
- **D3 - uniform factor, not a height-only factor:** the anchor says "reduce sprite HEIGHT to 1/2 current". A height-only factor would SQUASH the square 192x192 px atlas frames, so the world WIDTH follows the SAME 0.5 factor and the rendered HEIGHT is still exactly 1/2 of the previous height - the literal request is satisfied without distorting the art. The alternative (a width-only factor) would leave the height unchanged and would NOT satisfy the request. This is recorded as a non-blocking note for the user; the sprite ATLAS is not re-drawn and no new frames are authored.
- **D4 - one named lever, applied at the single choke point:** the factor lives in ONE exported constant, NEATRACING_PUBLIC_BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 0.5, and it is applied INSIDE computeBillboardScale (public.sprite.ts:705). That function is the only scale source for BOTH the placement footprint (billboardWorldHalfSize, public.sprite.ts:1843) and the rendered quad (buildBillboardUpload, right-world.pass.ts:887), so the two can never disagree. The module-private BILLBOARD_WORLD_SCALE = 1.0 is removed in the same slice, and the off-bleacher footprint probe at public.sprite.ts:1486-1489 is re-authored onto the named constant, because it currently reads the raw private constant and would otherwise diverge from the rendered size.
- **D5 - the duplicated meters-per-pixel twin is removed:** right-world.pass.ts:107 keeps a byte-for-byte copy of the public.sprite.ts meters-per-pixel constant (0.05). The constant is EXPORTED from public.sprite.ts and IMPORTED by the pass, and the local copy is deleted in the same slice (no deferred cleanup). Leaving two copies alive while introducing a third factor would create exactly the drift the step is meant to remove.
- **D6 - the AC-054 absolute clause is superseded, the RATIO clause is retained:** AC-054 required a billboard to render at the same world size as a same-world-size voxel. A uniform 0.5 factor breaks that absolute clause by design, while the perspective-parity RATIO clause (a distant sprite keeps the same relative size, because the shared focal/distance projection is untouched) stays green. The stale 1:1 assertions in public.sprite.test.ts are RE-AUTHORED in the slice that changes the constant, not deferred: the 1:1 test becomes a 1:2 test against the named constant, and the absolute same-world-size test becomes a named-constant-relative 1/2 assertion.
- **D7 - the personal space is NOT sprite-derived:** the 1 m personal space (NEATRACING_ROBOT_PERSONAL_SPACE_M in right-world.builder.ts) and the off-bleacher clearance (NEATRACING_PUBLIC_OFF_BLEACHER_PERSONAL_SPACE_CLEARANCE_M = 1 m - epsilon in public.sprite.ts) are FIXED constants. The halving makes the personal-space band MORE permissive (the sprites occupy less world area), which can only INCREASE the admitted crowd, never starve it - and the anchoring-capacity filter that governs the seated population is size-independent, so the 12-per-bleacher and 240-total counts are expected to stay exact. A RED guard asserts both, because a count drift must never be silently accepted.
- **D8 - distance independence is preserved:** computeBillboardScale keeps ignoring its distance argument. The perspective shrink of a distant crowd sprite stays the shared focal/distance projection, so the halving is a pure world-size change and not a second, competing per-distance scale (a per-distance factor would have broken the AC-054 RATIO contract and the projection parity with same-world-size voxels).
- **D9 - slice discipline:** four sequential slices, each within the <= 3 files and <= 4 h budget, strictly ordered because the slice files overlap: P1-sprite-scale-red-contracts (red-testing) -> P1-sprite-scale-world-factor (implementing, public.sprite.ts) -> P1-sprite-scale-render-quad (implementing, right-world.pass.ts) -> P1-sprite-scale-green (green-testing, trackers). The two implementation slices are SEPARATE so that the placement footprint and the rendered quad are never half-migrated by a single oversized edit, and each implementation slice owns the test file it changes.
- **D10 - green-light ownership:** this authoring instance does NOT grant the green light. A fresh 01-planning verification instance records the green light in the Latest validation evidence section before Step 14L enters execution; the authoring instance must not self-dispatch a patch cycle.

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** all four slices green; AC-077 proven by the focused suites and by the rendered-quad measurement; the AC-054 RATIO contract and the retained invariants re-asserted green; the visible-window smoke shows the crowd sprites at roughly human scale next to the car, still standing on the bleacher level, with the same counts and no atlas upload error; the coverage backlog, AC-PLN-003, README/Roadmap, and the handoff query updated.
- **Blocked:** a slice cannot meet its file or estimate budget, the halved footprint seats a spectator BELOW the bleacher surface or drops one to the ground, a crowd count drifts at any fixture seed, or the halving cannot be proven on the rendered quad - record the blocker in the Latest validation evidence section and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper. Never lower the 1/2 factor, the 12-per-bleacher count, or the 1 m personal space silently, and never let the sprite size drive the personal space.

**Required validation:**

- `npm run jest:base -- --testPathPatterns="examples/neatRacing/track|examples/neatRacing/engine"`
- `npx tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit`
- manual: `npm run build:neatRacing` + visible-window browser smoke on the served `/` page (the crowd sprites are visibly HALF their previous size, a seated spectator is about 4.8 m tall instead of 9.6 m and reads at roughly human scale next to the 1.2 m car, the seated spectators still stand ON the bleacher level, the seated count per bleacher is still 12, the off-bleacher walkers, standing spectators and team-colored mechanics are still present, the seated spectators still face TOWARD the car, and there is no WebGL atlas upload error)

PATCHED AGAIN 2026-10-26 by a fresh 01-planning (AUTHOR) instance after the VERIFICATION 2 recorded green-light: false with the NEW blocker B-9 (the RETAINED 290 km/h TRACTION_LOSS_MAX_SPEED_KMH ceiling) and the 7 non-blocking observations O-13..O-19: B-9 is CLOSED by adopting the 14N-rebaseline-risk.md D1.3 REPLACEMENT in the RED slice fixture criterion - the WHOLE D3.1 threshold table is dispositioned ROW BY ROW, the RETAINED NAMED CHECK proportionalTractionLoss KEEPS ITS NAME and CHANGES ITS SEMANTICS to the scale-free scrub-rate / speed-deficit form, the NEW named export NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SPEED_DEFICIT_KMH is owned by the tune-model slice, the ceiling is RE-PINNED above the scenario top speed so it stops being the binding constraint (the RB-4 inversion is absorbed by a NEW assertion and NEVER by deleting the check), and a measured deficit below the pinned floor BLOCKS the step and escalates via 00.cross-tier-helper instead of silently relaxing the floor; O-13..O-19 are FIXED (the two-pass measurement sequencing, the D1.2 J-number mapping, the 41-check supersession, the 5-to-6 file-count narrative, the D-10 supersession citation, the Q1 em dash in BOTH surfaces and the 31-figure rewording). (crisp = the car points decisively into the turn and the path is clearly different from where the car points; mushy = the car looks like it is just crabbing sideways)" (CRISP / MUSHY, the PRIMARY criterion - the 2026-10-24 verdict), Q3 "Does the countersteer CATCH the slide, or does it MIRROR it (the car snaps to the other side and keeps going)?" AMENDED 2026-10-26 by the 01-planning AUTHOR (PHASE-B MERGE): the feel DIRECTION is now DECIDED — **D-11: a BIGGER SLIDE** (the physical half of the feel; the crisper-recovery half is delivered by the countersteer catch) — and is RECORDED in this plan BEFORE any production edit, as the packet requires.

**Step objective:** Sharpen the drift FEEL on top of the mechanics Step 14G already closed: raise the slide prominence to the NAMED deterministic-proxy floor through the NAMED levers, re-derive the pose envelope so the articulation term can no longer break the derived bound, make the tire-gradient factor spread a measurable non-degenerate contract, re-baseline every pin the change legitimately invalidates (one ledger row per pin, no silent deletion), keep every Step 14G contract green, and close the step on the USER VISUAL GATE recorded on three surfaces.

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** physics|car|host, car.pass AND engine/lighting jest lanes green, neatRacing tsc clean, build passes, the visible-window smoke reports passed === true with EVERY named check in result.checks true, the MEASURED slide proxy, the sustained-tick count, the measured peak |pose|, the declared envelope 0.3050 rad and the tire-gradient factor spread are recorded, the RE-BASELINE LEDGER is complete with the measured values, and the USER VISUAL GATE verdict (with the bundle byte length and sha256) is recorded on THREE surfaces.
- **Blocked:** the slide prominence cannot be raised without degrading the low-speed handling or the determinism contract; or the measured peak |pose| exceeds the declared 0.3050 rad envelope (the MODEL is then at fault — the limit is NEVER widened); or the tire-gradient contract cannot be made non-degenerate without changing the user-approved body animation — record the blocker in Latest validation evidence and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper.

**PASS 2 — the RED-decided floor/ceiling decisions (the ones the packet asks the RED slice to decide).**

- **FLOOR — `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SPEED_DEFICIT_KMH` = 20 km/h.** A FLOOR, never a ceiling: the model must still bleed at least 20 km/h of speed across a 600-tick drift. The MEASURED current deficit is 112.26 km/h (M-28) and the projected new deficit is ≈ 28–46 km/h, so 20 km/h leaves headroom below the projection and still bites. **If the GREEN model lands below 20 km/h the MODEL is at fault — BLOCK + escalate, never relax the floor.**
- **CEILING — `TRACTION_LOSS_MAX_SPEED_KMH` = 340 km/h.** Strictly above the MEASURED top speed of 320.4 km/h (M-26) so the ceiling can gate a slide without gating the car's own top speed. The old 290 km/h was BELOW the top speed and was therefore inert.
- **FLOOR — `DRIFT_PROXY_MIN_RAD` = 0.05 rad** (= 0.25 × the exported 0.20 floor) and **HOLD — `DRIFT_PROXY_MIN_HOLD_FRAMES` = 120** (the engagement gate `DRIFT_PROXY_MIN_FRAMES` stays 3).

- **CEILING — `NEATRACING_TIRE_GRADIENT_MIN_SPREAD` = 0.5** against the MEASURED production spread 1.35.

**PASS 2 — the items this slice OWES to the green slice (recorded, not silently dropped).**

1. **The float32 precision correction (G-B).** The untouched monotonic test in `car.pass.test.ts` pins `toBeCloseTo(±DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_LIMIT_RAD, 10)`. At the 0.45 re-pin that precision is unreachable in float32: the MEASURED rendered value at 0.225 is 0.22500001091594907 (absDiff 1.09e-8) and at 0.1125 it is 3.02e-9. **The green/tune-model slice must relax that precision to 7 (the float32 epsilon) and add a re-baseline-ledger row.**
2. **`NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD` is still π/2 today**, so a constant-derived bound would be GREEN at HEAD. Home 2 therefore carries a local `DECLARED_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD = 0.45` literal alongside the contract; the tune-model slice must delete the literal when the export lands.
3. **`computeLongitudinalSpeedScrub` is required by G-5 but is NOT in the packet's new-export list** — it MUST be exported from `drift.model.ts` by the tune-model slice, or home 1's import-fails RED can never go green.
4. **The `reArmed` token** is in the plan's `DriftCommittedState {slip, turnSign, reArmed}` but NOT in the integration artifact's shape — the plan wins; the artifact must be reconciled.

            values), so a wrapped [-pi, pi) publication and a raw publication
            are BOTH accepted;
          - the integration keeps using that EXACT value, so the published
            field and the x/y advance can never diverge.

          (2) examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/chase-camera.ts (NEW in the
          green slice) exports EXACTLY these names:

              NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_FOLLOW_DT_S: number   // === 1/60
              NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_BACK: number          // 5.5
              NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_HEIGHT: number        // 2.4
              NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_LOOKAHEAD: number     // 8
              createChaseCameraFollowState(): ChaseCameraFollowState
              resolveChaseCameraAimRad(headingRad, followOffsetRad): number
              stepChaseCameraFollow(follow, step): ChaseCameraFollowState
              resolveChaseCameraBasis(carX, carY, aimRad): ChaseCameraBasis

          - ChaseCameraFollowState carries EXACTLY two fields:
            { offsetRad: number, lastTick: number };
          - the AIM LAW: the camera aim is the NOSE heading plus the follow
            offset, and the follow offset is the SIGNED SHORTEST-PATH delta
            between the PUBLISHED travel heading and the nose heading;
          - stepChaseCameraFollow takes a step descriptor
            { ticks: number, headingRad: number, travelHeadingRad: number,
              speedMps: number, tick: number } and returns the NEXT follow
            state; `ticks: 0` HOLDS the aim; a tick REGRESSION
            (tick < follow.lastTick) resets offsetRad to EXACTLY 0;
          - the per-tick follow change is PROPORTIONAL to speedMps times the
            shared drift amount (the user law S-1/S-4), NOT a fixed time
            constant (the retired NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_FOLLOW_TAU_S and
            NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_TRAVEL_AIM_GAIN names are FORBIDDEN and
            must not exist);

              lookTarget: [number, number, number],
              forwardVector: [number, number, number] };

            NEATRACING_CAR_SCENE_YAW_OFFSET_RAD (pi/2) stays EXPORTED from
            browser-entry.ts with its current value.

auto_expand: true
tdd_sequence: red-green
mode: fresh-session
source_of_truth: 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md + the verdict5-merged-gap-map record at the plan tail + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.audit-visuals.research.md (the 7-exist / 7-create wire ledger) + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.audit-physics.research.md (G-M5)'
copy_paste: true
next_step: 'the Step 14N USER GATE (AC-090) is re-run against the re-wired build; the 14P/14Q/14Q2/14R wave is the subject of the next verification pass and no execution is dispatched by this authoring pass'
pre_execute_hook:

  args:
    slice_id: 'P1-drift-presentation-red'
skills:
  - implementation-standards
  - red-test-contracts
  - green-validation-gates
  - spec-checklist
validation:
  - 'npm run jest:base -- --testPathPatterns="examples/neatRacing/physics|examples/neatRacing/car|examples/neatRacing/host"'
  - 'npx jest --testPathPatterns=examples/neatRacing/browser-entry'
  - 'npx tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit'
  - 'npx eslint examples/neatRacing/engine/passes/car.pass.ts examples/neatRacing/browser-entry/browser-entry.ts examples/neatRacing/host/hud.ts examples/neatRacing/host/race-session.ts'
  - 'npm run build:neatRacing'
  - 'manual: npm run build:neatRacing + visible-window browser smoke on the served game page (the HUD shows the traction readout, the tires change with the traction severity, and a car-to-car contact is actually RESOLVED on screen instead of passing through)'
  - 'manual: visible-window smoke fixture docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html - window.p1TurnDriftGreenSmokeResult.passed === true and EVERY named check in result.checks is true; the check COUNT is ASSERTED against the ACTUAL result.checks length at green time and is NEVER assumed'
acceptance_criteria:
  - 'AC-088 (RE-DERIVED 2026-10-27, verdict-5): the tire traction signal is REAL: the per-tire grip and the tire gradient are driven by the PUBLISHED traction severity (the ONE shared scalar from Step 14Q) and NOT by the fixed-sun lighting band (G-V4), and the front-wheel steer yaw is driven by the PHYSICS STATE and not by the raw steer echo (G-V5). The HUD shows a traction readout whose value is the published severity (the HUD state contract grows by the named field), and the drift seam carries the severity as its seventh field so the browser reads the SAME number as the car pass and the HUD. NO consumer re-derives the severity.'
  - 'AC-090 (the user gate is re-armed, NOT passed): this step does NOT close AC-090. The verdict of 2026-10-27 is REJECT (see plans/README.md and plans/Roadmap.md): the earlier fixture-iteration-4 close-out was scoped to the HARNESS (43 fixture checks) and was NEVER an AC-090 pass. The AC-090 questions are the six verbatim questions in plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.14N-fixture-gate.md section 5.3 and they are RE-ASKED against the re-wired build, in MANUAL mode, on the road, with the camera reading the travel direction. The six answers are recorded in the fixture-gate artifact and the verdict is recorded by the USER (or by a fresh verification instance that is explicitly authorised to record the user verdict), NEVER by an implementation or a green-testing slice.'
  - 'AC-089 (RE-DERIVED 2026-10-27, verdict-5): the live collision path is RE-WIRED: the car-to-car resolver is called from the live tick, so a contact is actually resolved on screen (today the resolver is imported by NO production module - the live path is DEAD). The re-baselined pins get ONE ledger row each in THIS PLAN (the CarPassCarState contract, the HUD state contract, the seam count 7 to 8, the fixture count 45 to 46), and the PRESERVE SET (the determinism twin-runs, the straight-line exact zeros, the AC-047D byte-identity re-anchored on the PRODUCTION serializer, the 24 non-drift fixture checks) stays green.'

**THE EIGHTH SEAM FIELD IS A NAMED CHANNEL, NEVER THE SEVERITY.** The eighth field is `poseRateRadPerS` - the PUBLISHED pose-spring RATE (rad/s), READ from `car.drift.pose.poseRate` and NEVER re-derived in the browser. WHY THIS CHANNEL: the browser half is RENDER-RATE dependent (the host releases 0-4 simulation ticks per rendered frame), so a frame difference measures the CAMERA, not the car - the published rate is the crab own per-tick quantity, so the fixture can measure the ring-down and the far-side pop in SIMULATION time next to the pose it belongs to.

**THE HUD READOUT CONTRACT (the equality band, not a vacuous equality).** The 46th check compares the HUD's rendered percent against the seam's published severity and accepts the **absolute display-quantization band of +/- 0.5 points**, NOT `ratio == 1`: a severity of `0.004` renders as `0%`, so a strict equality would be a false failure. The ratio is published as EVIDENCE only, and the check asserts that at least one sample was actually paired, so it cannot pass vacuously. The DOM read and the seam read are taken at the **SAME INSTANT** (the phase sampler pairs them in one frame), so the comparison is not a cross-frame race.

THE TURN-RATE DIMENSION IS ASSERTED AS WELL, NOT ONLY THE SPEED DIMENSION: for the SAME speed and the SAME steer axis, a STRICTLY LARGER demanded turn rate produces a STRICTLY DEEPER committed slide, and a ZERO demanded turn rate produces an EXACTLY 0 committed slide AT ENGAGEMENT (an UNCOMMITTED latch) even at the top speed - the zero-rate lane is asserted FROM A FRESH STATE, because a ZERO demand under a LIVE latch HOLDS the committed depth instead of zeroing it. THE LATCH-HOLD CLAUSE IS A SEPARATE LANE AND IS ASSERTED AS WELL (FP-14S-03): once the latch is live, a ZERO momentum demand HOLDS the committed depth (the slide NEVER SNAPS to zero under a live latch) and only the RELEASE - the countersteer or the NEUTRAL wheel - unwinds it; the ENGAGEMENT-scoped zero lane and the LIVE-LATCH HOLD lane are DISTINCT lanes and BOTH are asserted, so the zero clause can never be carried by a fresh-state-only lane. THE MIRRORED-CONSTANT GUARD IS ASSERTED: at the SAME speed and the SAME steer axis of the STRICT-DEEPER LANE (the lane whose explicit rate is NOT the mirror), the ABSENT-rate lane (the demanded turn rate field OMITTED, so the law falls back to the mirrored steer-times-speed-percent rate) MUST read a DIFFERENT committed slide from the STRICTLY-LARGER explicit-rate lane, because the SMALLER explicit rate IS the mirror of the production fallback rate (the fallback is steer * NEATRACING_DRIFT_FULL_STEER_TURN_RATE_RAD_PER_S * the speed percent - drift.model.ts:877) and a lane the MIRROR alone can satisfy does NOT discriminate the law - without the guard the strict-deeper relation would rest on ONE lane only, and a law that IGNORED the explicit demanded turn rate would still satisfy the smaller lane; the guard is asserted BEFORE the relational clause. The contract opens with a NON-VACUITY GUARD in the Step 14Q style: BOTH lanes must REALLY slide (a zero slide would satisfy the strict-deeper clause vacuously) and the guard is asserted BEFORE the relational clause. The demanded turn rate is expressed through a WIDENED LOCAL VIEW of the internal drift input (the Step 14R red-slice residual (2) lesson - the field is an internal TYPE MEMBER, so a MISSING-IMPORT failure is UNSATISFIABLE for it) and the field name is pinned by this contract, never by a placeholder export. Today the commitment is a COMMAND: the 0.5 engage gate opens the latch and the slide ramps at the speed-proportional ENTRY RATE (drift.model.ts:758, :781 and :788), so the momentum is ABSENT - the RED must re-open the command law explicitly, exactly as the Step 14Q RED re-opened the speed-blind grip budget.         text: 'drift.model.test.ts asserts that the momentum demand EXISTS and is a FUNCTION of the demanded turn rate (at a ZERO demanded turn rate the demand is EXACTLY 0 and at a NON-ZERO demanded turn rate it is STRICTLY GREATER than 0, at the SAME speed), so a law that is only a clamp or only a bound can NEVER pass this contract. The BOUND clauses are PRESERVATION GUARDS and are LABELLED as such: the momentum demand can NEVER push the committed slide past the declared depth budget (NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD) and the published traction severity stays inside the closed unit interval at the saturation speed - BOTH clauses hold today (the depth clamp at drift.model.ts:817 and the severity clamp at :624) and are NOT counted as reds: they are the RAILS the new cause must stay on. The contract opens with a NON-VACUITY GUARD in the Step 14Q style: the non-zero demanded turn rate lane must REALLY produce a demand above 0 and the guard is asserted BEFORE the bound clauses. The RED slice also MEASURES and RECORDS the feasible window for the momentum budget (the analogue of the Step 14Q gain window [0.386, 0.5]) - the window is measured, never carried.'
      - id: 'RED-4 (the live tick APPLIES the momentum)'
        text: 'physics.step.service.test.ts asserts that the LIVE tick APPLIES the momentum law: the service RESOLVES the demanded turn rate ONCE per tick and the SAME resolved number feeds BOTH the yaw and the momentum law - the drift commitment call site RECEIVES that number and there is NEVER a second re-derivation - so the law is APPLIED end-to-end and not merely exported. THIS IS THE ONE DISCRIMINATING CLAUSE OF THIS CONTRACT AND IT WAS RED WHEN IT WAS AUTHORED: at the service level the drift commitment was fed EXACTLY SIX fields (the steer, the speed, the speed percent, the dt, the lateral velocity and the slip angle - the pre-14S service, physics.step.service.ts:458-464 in that tree), so the drift NEVER saw a demanded turn rate at all, and the yaw resolved its OWN per-tick delta in a SEPARATE place (resolveYawRatePerTick - the pre-14S call site was physics.step.service.ts:700-706; the function itself is now at :752) - the two therefore did NOT share one resolved number. ON THE CURRENT TREE the clause is GREEN ON ARRIVAL in the production (the demanded turn rate is resolved ONCE at physics.step.service.ts:459, the yaw per-tick delta is DERIVED from it at :463 and the SAME number feeds the commitment at :480 and :487), and the clause STAYS in the contract, because the contract is the SERVICE-LEVEL statement that the law is APPLIED end-to-end and not merely exported. THE UNIT OF THE DEMANDED TURN RATE IS PINNED BY THIS CONTRACT: the existing yaw law resolves a PER-TICK DELTA (radians per tick) and a per-tick delta and a rate are NOT interchangeable (a unit mismatch is a silent factor-of-sixty error), so the RED slice RECORDS the chosen unit and its basis, the service resolves THAT unit ONCE per tick, the momentum law consumes it, and the yaw per-tick delta is DERIVED from the SAME resolved number so the yaw behaviour stays BIT-IDENTICAL (this step changes the DRIFT only - the turn-rate law itself is Step 14T work). **User instruction:** (2026-10-28 verdict-6, relayed by the orchestrator) — the car's weight at high speed must be what causes the drift when turning; a momentum law is critical and entirely missing today, and from playing the build the only thing that is noticed is an annoying camera effect.

**Step objective:** Make the drift a CONSEQUENCE of the momentum instead of a command from the wheel: the committed slide is produced by the momentum excess (the lateral acceleration the commanded turn demands minus the lateral acceleration the tires can hold at that speed), so the same wheel command slides deeper the faster the car goes, the slide is exactly zero at a standstill, and the old entry-rate command law is deleted in the same change that introduces the new one.

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** the physics lane and the car-pass lane are green, the neatRacing tsc is clean, the eslint lane is clean, the build passes, the momentum ledger rows are written in this plan, the old entry-rate command law is DELETED, and the PRESERVE SET is still green.
- **Blocked:** the momentum law cannot deepen the slide with the speed without breaching the depth budget, the severity bound or the PRESERVE SET — record the blocker in Latest validation evidence and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper; the PRESERVE SET is NEVER relaxed, the severity bound is NEVER widened and the depth budget is NEVER raised to make a contract pass.

**Required validation:**

- The consolidated `slice-advancement` gate for the Step 14S packet (run ONCE; the constituent gates are never run individually).
- `node scripts/agent-customization/validate-plan-sync.mjs --plan=plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md`

**User instruction:** (2026-10-28 verdict-6, relayed by the orchestrator) — turning is also too sharp: the turning rate should reduce slightly and proportionally to speed, not too much as that would prevent turning or drifting, but it helps convey the feeling of speed. AI agents may have a turning rate by %, which gives them full control, but the user arrow inputs need a little turning rate adjustment to make the car more controllable and fun to play.

**Step objective:** Give the turn rate a mild, speed-proportional reduction that never prevents turning or drifting, and separate the two turn-input laws on the same steer axis: the AI owns a turn-rate-percent channel with full control, while the user arrow channel carries only the mild adjustment.

**User instruction:** (2026-10-30 AC-090 VERDICT 6 - REJECT, relayed by the orchestrator) — track should be wider on corners on the outer part of the curve, to give space for the drift.

**Step objective:** Give the track edge an inner and an outer half-width instead of one symmetric half-width, so the drift room is added on the outside of every corner and the road never narrows on the inside.

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** the four edge contracts are green by name, the three track/physics readers resolve the edge through the same seam, the retired symmetric read is deleted from those readers, the band ladder keeps its constants and its cumulative semantics on the new measurement base, the invalidated literals are re-pinned, the preserve set is still green, and the edge ledger rows are written in this plan.
- **Blocked:** the outer-only widening cannot be derived from the existing track geometry, or the containment bound cannot follow the widened edge without breaking the AC-081 pose-independence / one-bound / shipped-tick / anti-masking clauses — record the blocker in Latest validation evidence and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper; a symmetric edge is NEVER kept as a workaround and the preserve set is NEVER relaxed.

**Required validation:**

- The consolidated `slice-advancement` gate for the Step 14U packet (run ONCE; the constituent gates are never run individually).
- `node scripts/agent-customization/validate-plan-sync.mjs --plan=plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md`

THE RE-AUTHORING SCOPE SPLIT (RECORDED ON ALL THREE SURFACES THE MANDATE NAMES - this wave note, the Phase-1 step list row for Step 14W and the plan tail): the AI lane file examples/neatRacing/physics/ai.autopilot.test.ts is owned by the slice that applies the moved bound in the shipped tick (P1-sand-service), because the moved bound IS the production change that can invalidate the AI lane literals and the retired road-edge contracts, and a re-pin (and a retired-contract re-authoring) NEVER leaves the step (and NEVER the slice) that owns the production change that invalidated it (the Step 14Q precedent); the three in-file-set test files stay with P1-sand-repin. THIS STEP DOES NOT GREEN-LIGHT ANYTHING, FLIPS NO STATUS AND DISPATCHES NOTHING.'

acceptance_criteria:
  - 'AC-094 (a - the boundary law NEVER carries the car to the middle of the track): touching the edge NEVER RESEATS the car on the ribbon and NEVER resets its longitudinal progress. THE CONTRACT IS WRITTEN AGAINST THE OBSERVABLE (the measured displacement between the pre-bound pose and the published pose), NOT against a guessed mechanism, and the RED slice RECORDS the CLASSIFICATION (BOUNDARY/MODEL) and the MEASURED displacement BEFORE any production edit. THE USER-NAMED BEHAVIOUR IS THE ONLY SOURCE OF TRUTH: the car may leave the road, but the boundary law may not move it to the middle of the track.'
  - 'AC-094 (b - the off-track band is DRIVABLE): the road is followed by a NAMED, BOUNDED off-road band (the sand band) on which the car CONTINUES TO DRIVE and is NEVER pushed back onto the road. THE BAND IS THE REGION BETWEEN THE DRIVABLE EDGE AND THE OUTER EDGE OF THE EXISTING NAMED GRASS APRON, so the band width is an EXISTING published constant and NEVER a band-paint constant (AC-080 keeps the tri-colour ladder a PAINT ladder: no ladder constant becomes a physical bound). A CAR THAT HAS CROSSED THE EDGE REALLY ENDS UP OFF THE ROAD (its lateral distance from the centreline exceeds the drivable half-width after the crossing tick) - the road edge is an inner boundary, never a wall.'
  - 'AC-094 (c - the band is SAND-LIKE): the speed on the band is reduced by the EXISTING NAMED OFF-ROAD LAW (the existing off-road deceleration constant and the existing off-road speed-floor constant) and that law is REACHABLE IN THE LIVE TICK, because the surface is resolved from the POST-MOVE pose (today the surface is resolved at the tick start, so the off-road machinery is unreachable). THE BAND SPEED IS MEASURED by the RED slice and RECORDED in this plan: it is STRICTLY LOWER than the road speed for the same deterministic input and the car KEEPS ROLLING (the band is never a standstill). NO NEW SPEED CONSTANT IS AUTHORED BY THIS WAVE and the sand-LIKE FEEL is judged by the USER gate, never by an author-chosen number.'
  - 'AC-094 (d - the bound MOVES, it does not disappear): there is exactly ONE containment bound and it is now the OUTER edge of the sand band (the car may not leave the band), and it KEEPS the AC-081 POSE-INDEPENDENCE clause (the bound reads the ribbon geometry ONLY - never the heading, the slip or the drift pose), the ONE-BOUND clause and the SHIPPED-TICK clause (the bound is applied in the shipped tick after the translation and before the publish). THE RETIRED ROAD-EDGE BOUND IS DELETED in the slice that re-bases it (NO deferred cleanup): a reader that keeps the retired road-edge bound would be a second, competing containment.'
  - 'AC-094 (e - ONE surface model): the physics classifier and the rasterizer agree on the band boundary - a point on the band is the SAME surface in both models - and the band REUSES the EXISTING grass surface member (the surface union stays road | curb | grass, so no exhaustive surface switch elsewhere can break).'
  - 'AC-094 (f - the 10 m prop clearance is NOT the band): the band reaches a few metres past the road edge and the right-world props stand at least 10 m past the edge (AC-096), so the two rules never overlap and the band is not a prop zone.'
  - 'AC-094 (g - the AI lane is RE-AUTHORED IN THIS STEP, NEVER deferred): the AI lane file examples/neatRacing/physics/ai.autopilot.test.ts is owned by the slice that applies the moved bound in the shipped tick (P1-sand-service) and the AI lanes the moved bound invalidates are RE-AUTHORED IN THIS SAME STEP against the moved bound: the lane names name the BAND bound, the asserted observable changes from "reseated onto the drivable edge" to "contained at the band outer edge", and the anti-masking clause (AC-085) is KEPT - the lane must keep being able to FAIL. A retired contract is NEVER simply deleted and NEVER left asserting the retired behaviour. THE RE-AUTHORING IS NEVER DEFERRED to a later step: it travels with the production change that invalidated it (the Step 14Q precedent), so NO carry-forward into Step 14Y remains, and the split of the re-authoring scope is RECORDED on all three surfaces the mandate names (the step wave note, the Phase-1 step list and the plan tail).'
  - 'AC-081 (RECONCILED by this re-open wave - the RETAINED half and the SUPERSEDED half are both named): RETAINED - the POSE-INDEPENDENCE clause, the ONE-BOUND clause, the SHIPPED-TICK clause (applyTrackContainment applies the bound after the translation and before the publish, with the live binding in browser-entry.ts), the anti-masking clause (AC-085) and the "the bound reads the ribbon geometry ONLY" clause. SUPERSEDED IN PART - the clause "leaving the track is NO LONGER ALLOWED behaviour" and the clause that the grass apron is a NON-drivable OFF-ROAD band only: the road is followed by a NAMED, BOUNDED, DRIVABLE off-road band (the sand band) on which the car KEEPS DRIVING with a sand-like slowdown, and the bound moves to the OUTER edge of that band. THE BOUND LAW NEVER RESEATS THE CAR ON THE RIBBON.'
  - 'AC-090 (the user gate is NOT claimed): this step does NOT close AC-090 and records NO AC-090 verdict. The 2026-10-30 verdict stays REJECT; the five verbatim USER directives are re-asked by the USER in MANUAL mode on the road AFTER Step 14X and Step 14Y. The browser lane stays WAIVED-not-passed under the standing NO-browser user mandate and NO served-page evidence is claimed by this step.'

      - id: 'RED-2 (the band is DRIVABLE - the car really ends up off the road)'

      - id: 'RED-3 (the band is SAND-LIKE and the off-road law is REACHABLE in the live tick)'

THE BAND SPEED IS MEASURED HERE and RECORDED in the plan (the road speed, the band speed and the difference for the same input); NO band-speed NUMBER is carried into the contract text and NO new speed constant is authored by this wave.'

**User instruction:** (2026-10-30 AC-090 VERDICT 6 - REJECT, relayed by the orchestrator) — touching the edge teleports you to the middle of the track, I didn't asked for that, cars can go off track, but it goes slow, as if on sand.

**Step objective:** Turn the road edge from a wall into the inner edge of a drivable, sand-like off-road band, and move the single containment bound to the outer edge of that band — without ever carrying the car to the middle of the track.

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** the boundary law never reseats the car on the ribbon and never resets longitudinal progress, a car that crosses the edge really ends up off the road, the band surface is reachable in the live tick and the measured band speed is strictly lower than the measured road speed while the car keeps rolling, the one bound sits at the band outer edge with its pose-independence, one-bound and shipped-tick clauses, the classifier and the rasterizer agree on the band boundary, the retired-bound lanes are re-authored in this same step, and the boundary ledger rows are written in this plan.
- **Blocked:** the moved bound cannot keep the car inside the band without reintroducing a reseat, or the retired-bound contracts cannot be re-authored one-for-one inside the 3-file cap — record the named conflict in Latest validation evidence and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper; the bound is NEVER dropped and the reseat is NEVER reintroduced.

**Required validation:**

- The consolidated `slice-advancement` gate for the Step 14W packet (run ONCE; the constituent gates are never run individually).
- `node scripts/agent-customization/validate-plan-sync.mjs --plan=plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md`

**User instruction:** (2026-10-30 AC-090 VERDICT 6 - REJECT, relayed by the orchestrator) — the "drift" camera effect is terrible, too sensitive, snaps back horrible, doesn't look like drifting and it makes the camera tilt too much (cap at half or less) and too fast (much slower than now). I couldnt even test how the actual drift feels.

**Step objective:** Desensitise the chase camera, cap the aim offset at half of its measured pre-wave peak or less, slow the response down and delete the multiplicative snap-back — leaving the drift physics and the published state untouched.

**Stop conditions:**

- **Done:** the offset never exceeds the named cap, the follow gain is lower and the time-to-cap longer than the measured pre-wave values, the release is monotonic and inside the named smooth fraction, the snap-back enabler is deleted at its source, every reader sees the capped offset, the preserve set is still green, the fixture checks are authored (not run), and the camera ledger rows are written in this plan.
- **Blocked:** the cap or the smoother release cannot be implemented without changing the published state or the drift physics — record the named conflict in Latest validation evidence and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper; the camera is never allowed to change the drift model.

**Required validation:**

- The consolidated `slice-advancement` gate for the Step 14X packet (run ONCE; the constituent gates are never run individually).
- `node scripts/agent-customization/validate-plan-sync.mjs --plan=plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md`

## Validation gates

Step-level `validation` lists inside each packet are the authoritative per-step command
sources (MCP allowlist authority: `active-step.validation`). Consolidated gate routing:

- `slice-advancement` — consolidates plan-sync + step-packet + plan-slice-quality +
  plan-command-lint + shared-validation + code-coverage + specialist-review; run per
  active slice/step handoff. The Step 01 authoring pass is captured in
  `## Latest validation evidence`.
- `cortex-index` — RAG freshness + workflow/ corpus MCP liveness; rerun after every
  tracker edit batch (see `rag-index/reindex-plan-family.mjs` + `build-index` +
  `validate-index` recovery loop).
- `agent-graph` — only after any agent delegation change. `learning-event` — only after
  discovering a workflow gap or improvement.

## Deferred questions

None. The spec records all open questions RESOLVED (section 20); the tracker introduces
no new NEEDS CLARIFICATION markers. If execution uncovers a spec conflict, stop and
escalate via `00.cross-tier-helper` before deviating.

- **RESOLVED (2026-10-26, Step 14N PHASE-B MERGE) — the drift-feel DIRECTION.** DECIDED as **D-11: A BIGGER SLIDE** (the PHYSICAL half of the feel; the crisper-recovery half is delivered by the model itself, through the countersteer catch). The decision is recorded in this plan in the `## PlanUpdate - Step 14N PHASE-B MERGE (01-planning AUTHOR, 2026-10-26)` block, BEFORE any production edit, with its named lever (`NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SLIDE_PROXY_RAD` over the DETERMINISTIC unit proxy `computeDriftSlideProxyRad(slipAngleRad) = |slip| * |GAIN - 1|`, recommended 0.20 rad) and its coupled constraint (`NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD >= 0.40` at `GAIN = 0.5`). The RED slice `P1-drift-feel-red` pins the DECIDED direction and may still choose the exact in-band VALUES; it must NOT reopen the direction inside 14N. The 2026-10-24 question is therefore CLOSED and is retained here for the audit trail.
- **OPEN (2026-10-26, Step 14N) — the canopy desync.** `examples/neatRacing/engine/passes/glass.pass.ts` reads `car.yawRad` only and never the drift pose (integration proposal R-03), so a 0.3050 rad (17.5 deg) body slide is a canopy error. Measured on the real pipeline (8 fixture seeds, seated billboards only): level-major → `levelsTouched = 2` at EVERY seed, per-level `[4,2,0] / [4,4,0] / [5,2,0] / [5,5,0] / [5,5,0] / [5,4,0] / [5,3,0]`, level index 2 receiving ZERO sprites; level-interleaved → `levelsTouched = 3` at EVERY seed, per-level `[2,2,2] / [3,2,2] / [3,3,2] / [3,2,2] / [4,4,4] / [4,4,3] / [3,3,3] / [3,3,3]`. Measured shortfall envelope (8 fixture seeds x EVERY bleacher x the front row of EVERY level): the nominal 1 m spacing computes to `0.99999999999997014` .. `1.0000000000000195` — a worst-case shortfall of **2.99e-14 m** and a worst-case overshoot of **1.95e-14 m** — and at seed 4242 bleacher[2] ALL SIX gaps of a level fall below 1.0. | the momentum-law consumer relation | the softened turn must still open a slide | CLEAN - the top-speed softened user turn STILL commits a slide (`[RED-14T-2-TOP-SPEED-SLIDE-COMMITS]` is GREEN), the AC-047A 0.2 rad floor STILL holds (0.2740512045422142 rad at 56 m/s) and the drift model's turn SIGN is `Math.sign(steer)`, never the rate. |
| the BIT-IDENTITY invariant (AC-091) | the yaw delta must come from the SAME resolved rate | CLEAN - the rate is resolved ONCE (`resolveDemandedTurnRateRadPerS`, `:524`), the per-tick delta is DERIVED from it (`resolveYawRatePerTick`, `:889`, `rate * dt`), the published `yawRate` IS that same per-tick delta (`:649`) and the drift commitment CONSUMES the same number (`:546`, `:553`). The delta is NEVER recovered by dividing delta/dt. |

  observations:
    - id: OBS-1
      severity: BLOCKER

    - id: OBS-2
      severity: BLOCKER
      report: 'AC-055B frozen animation: selectPublicWalkFrame called with timeSeconds=0 at build time — walk cycle renders a single static pose.'
    - id: OBS-3
      severity: BLOCKER
      report: 'AC-055C gaze frozen: bleacher spectators and mechanics pick look-at-car frames relative to the static default camera position instead of the live car/camera position.'
    - id: OBS-4
      severity: MAJOR
      report: 'Render-state leak: billboard scope leaves CULL_FACE disabled (never restored), leaves program/buffer/texture/attrib arrays bound, does not reset state downstream passes may assume.'
    - id: OBS-5
      severity: MINOR
      report: 'Atlas UV Y-flip relies on implicit quad UV mapping (logical row 0 at data row 0, v=v0 at top). Add an explicit comment/contract note (and UNPACK_FLIP_Y_WEBGL if the GL state requires it) so orientation cannot silently break.'
    - id: OBS-6
      severity: BLOCKER
      report: 'USER OBSERVED 2026-10-18 (~20:40-04:00): ALL robot sprites render upside down (180 degrees vertically) on the live page. The atlas-to-quad V mapping is actually inverted in practice, not merely fragile — OBS-5 escalates from a contract note to a BLOCKER behavior fix.'
  directed_fix:
    - 'Move runtime frame selection into the per-frame draw path: the pass draw() must recompute per-billboard frame selection (direction id vs live camera/car, walk frame vs live clock, look-at-car) each frame using preallocated scratch storage (reuse the existing nearest-first scratch buffer pattern).     - 'Feed the walk cycle from the existing per-frame clock input the pass already receives (or add one monotonic seconds input to draw()); walk cycle period must be slow (>= 2.4s per cycle) and deterministic given the same clock. Zero per-frame allocation (no object/array creation in draw path).'
    - 'Look-at-car gaze: recompute direction id each frame from billboard world position -> live car position (mechanics + seated spectators); non-seated walkers keep facing their walk heading while walking and glance at the car only on deterministic pause intervals (slow look-around is allowed for a minority — most crowd gazes the car).'
    - 'Restore render state after the billboard draw scope: re-enable CULL_FACE to the pre-pass state (read it, then restore), unbind texture from unit 0, useProgram(null), and disable the attrib arrays the billboard program enabled, mirroring conventions of other engine passes.'

    - 'Lanes must stay green: npm run jest:base -- --testPathPatterns="examples/neatRacing/track|examples/neatRacing/engine"; npx tsc -p tsconfig.neatRacing.json --noEmit.'

<!-- fix-packet-P1-starfield-horizon-iteration-3 -->

```yaml
fix_packet:
  id: fix-packet-P1-starfield-horizon-iteration-3
  reported_by: 14H-sf-review3 (webgl2-glsl-render-reviewer, fresh re-review) REQUEST_CHANGES on fix-packet-P1-starfield-horizon-iteration-2
  status: CLOSED
  goal: fix-starfield-ndc-mapping
  observations:
    - 'OBS-G (HIGH, verified by orchestrator grep 2026-10-19T22:5x): the GLSL vertex shader in starfield.pass.ts computes ndcX = (wrappedXPx / u_backdropSizePx.x) * 2.0 - 1.0, but wrappedXPx lives in TILE space [0, 512) while u_backdropSizePx.x is the computed backing width (1280..1920). With tileWidth=512 and backdropWidth=1280 the rightmost star lands at ndcX ~= -0.2 (left ~40% of the viewport; left ~27% at 1920). This is the TRUE root cause of OBS-F left-only coverage: the iteration-2 change (computed backing width as denominator) actively squashed the field to the left fraction. Fix: the NDC draw mapping must stretch the 512-px GENERATION tile across the full NDC width - divide by u_tileSizePx (the generation tile size), NOT by u_backdropSizePx; expected result ndcX spans the full [-1, +1) range with the uniform star distribution. Apply the same invariance to the vertical mapping (ndcY denominator must be u_tileSizePx.y, not u_backdropSizePx.y) so the [1, u_horizonNdcY] mapping holds for any backdrop height, not only when they happen to be equal.'
    - 'OBS-H (MEDIUM, verified by orchestrator grep): setBackdropSize(widthPx, heightPx) only re-uploads u_backdropSizePx via uniform2f; it does NOT regenerate or re-clamp the star placements even though placement clamping uses min(tileHeightPx, backdropHeightPx). ```yaml
plan_update:
  slice_id: 'P1-crowd-facing-relative'
  fix_packet_id: 'fix-packet-P1-crowd-facing-relative-iteration-1'
  step: 'Step 14J'
  status: REOPENED
  role: '04-implementing'
  iteration: 1
  reviewer: 'webgl2-glsl-render-reviewer (dispatched by review-coordinator)'
  verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES
  blocking_findings:
    - id: 'F1'
      file: 'examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.ts'
      location: 'resolveCameraRelativeDirectionIndex - the relativeYaw line'
      finding: 'The conversion transplants the Neatenstein CCW-compass algebra (relativeYaw = cameraYaw + PI - facingYaw) onto the neatRacing compass (yaw = atan2(dx, dz), 0 rad = +Z). The lateral sense is therefore MIRRORED: a spectator whose nose points to the camera SCREEN-RIGHT resolves to index 6 (left) instead of index 2 (right). Front and back are unaffected, so the RED-A assertions alone could not detect it.'
      evidence:
        - 'browser-entry.ts lookAtInto sets the view xAxis to (-fZ, 0, fX): the camera right axis is the forward axis rotated -90 deg in the neatRacing compass, so a robot facing screen-right has facingYaw = cameraYaw - 90 deg.'
        - 'right-world.pass.ts uploads the atlas rows verbatim (no U flip) and the billboard quad maps u1 (image-right) onto +cameraRight, so image-right equals screen-right.'
        - 'examples/neatenstein/robot-sprite-data.js: the right frame (line 429) puts the visor on the IMAGE-right side of the head and the left frame (line 1237) is its exact mirror, so index 2 means nose toward screen-right.'
      required_change: 'relativeYaw = facingYaw - cameraYaw + Math.PI, which yields 0 = front (faces the camera), 2 = right (screen-right), 4 = back, 6 = left (screen-left). Correct the helper JSDoc: state the neatRacing-compass form, the art anchor, and that the Neatenstein algebra is mirrored because Neatenstein uses the opposite (CCW) compass handedness.'
    - id: 'F2'
      file: 'examples/neatRacing/track/public.sprite.test.ts'
      location: 'expectedCameraRelativeDirection (lines 191-208) plus its doc block (lines 171-190); the EXPECTED NEW API doc block (lines 210-235)'
      finding: 'The RED expectation helper re-implements the implementation algebra, so it is tautological and can never detect a mirror; and its doc premise is factually wrong (a camera looking toward +Z keeps seeing the world +X direction on its own right). In neatRacing the camera right axis is (-fZ, 0, fX), so a +Z-looking camera sees world +X on its LEFT.'
      required_change: 'Re-derive the expectation GEOMETRICALLY from the camera basis with no shared yaw algebra: f = normalize(cameraForward.xz), r = (-fZ, 0, fX), d = normalize(gazeTarget - robotPosition), along = d dot f, lateral = d dot r, phi = atan2(lateral, along), index = round(((PI - phi) mod 2PI) / 45deg) mod 8. Correct the misleading doc blocks and add a LATERAL contract: a spectator facing the car due south renders as left for a camera forward of [1,0,0] and as right for [-1,0,0], asserted on BOTH the runtime and the build-time path. The two RED-A assertions (front for a north heading, 2-step circular distance for a 90 deg heading change) must NOT be weakened or removed.'
  non_blocking_findings:
    - 'F3: artifacts/shared-validation.json is stale; the visible-window smoke and the artifact regeneration belong to 05-green-testing (P1-crowd-green).'
    - 'F4: the build-time gaze target is the camera position while the runtime gaze target is the car position. Accepted as a follow-on note (the build-time path approximates the chase rig); no change in this slice.'
    - 'F5: RESOLVED - the basis derivation cameraUp x cameraRight = cameraForward is the exact inverse of the browser-entry basis, so browser-entry.ts and frame-composer.ts MUST NOT be edited.'
    - 'F6: the frame-composer draw-state bag defaults imply a 180 deg-wrong forward before the first basis update; follow-on note for the 05-green-testing visible-window smoke.'
  fix_loop:
