```yaml
fix_packet:
  id: fix-packet-P1-crowd-row-level-host-iteration-1
  slice_id: P1-crowd-row-level-host
  status: FIXED
  goal: address-requested-changes
  iteration: 1
  source: 'determinism-reviewer (Tier-3, dispatched through review-coordinator; severity FULL, specialistCount 1), iteration 1 verdict REQUEST_CHANGES'
  observations:
    - 'OBS-F1 (MEDIUM, blocking): NO FALSIFIABLE TEST proved the B5 RNG-stream preservation. The one-shot bleacher reservation must consume the SAME number of PRNG draws as the unreserved path; if it skipped or added a draw, every downstream prop placement would drift and the right world would stop being reproducible for a given seed. The implementation as reviewed had no test that could fail if the draw were skipped.'
    - 'OBS-F2 (MEDIUM, blocking): the "deterministic slot" assertion was a TAUTOLOGY - it re-derived the reserved slot with the SAME algorithm the production code uses, so it could never fail and proved nothing.'
    - 'OBS-F3 (non-blocking): no SCENE-LEVEL same-seed stability assertion existed. The builder-level emission was asserted, but the ASSEMBLED scene (props + billboards + host selection) was not asserted to be identical across two builds of the same seed.'
    - 'OBS-F4 (non-blocking): the plan text said "declare the first outer-ring slot a bleacher" while the implementation reserves the MAX-GAP slot. The plan wording was reconciled rather than the code bent to the wording, because the first outer-ring slot SHARES its track station with the first inner-ring slot.'
    - 'OBS-F5 (non-blocking): the reserved-slot rule was not documented as SEED-DEPENDENT (through the track geometry) and the gap UNIT (spline-sample index space, not metres and not arc length) was undisclosed.'
    - 'OBS-C1 (coordinator-only): artifacts/shared-validation.json was STALE - it carried the 2-file changed set of a PRIOR slice and a prior timestamp, so the specialist reviewed against evidence that did not describe this slice.'
    - 'OBS-C2 (coordinator-only): the specialist-review gate evidence resolved to a DIFFERENT plan than the one under implementation.'
    - 'OBS-N1 (non-blocking, iteration 2): the B5 stream-preservation rationale was MIS-DESCRIBED. It claimed that a skipped archetype draw at the reserved slot would shift "every downstream prop placement". In the REACHABLE track space that claim is VACUOUS: the reserved slot is ALWAYS the terminal outer slot, so a skipped draw there has NO later prop to shift and the only observable difference is the reserved bleacher OWN colour draw (a probabilistic 1 - (1/4)^4 = 255/256 signal). The deterministic teeth of the B5 contract therefore had to be moved to a seam where the reserved slot is NOT terminal.'
    - 'OBS-N2 (non-blocking, iteration 2): the reachable track geometry was not pinned anywhere, so the reachability fact behind OBS-N1 was an unstated assumption.'
    - 'OBS-N3 (non-blocking, iteration 2): one reserved-slot assertion was a TAUTOLOGY - it compared selectBleacherReservationSlot(100, 2, 8) with itself and could never fail.'
    - 'OBS-N4 (non-blocking, iteration 2): the OBS-F1 PRNG-chain description mixed the mixing steps into one parenthetical, leaving the ORDER of the operations ambiguous.'
    - 'OBS-N5 (coordinator-owned gate defect, iteration 2): the specialist-review GATE itself was defective for long multi-step plans. scripts/agent-customization/gates/specialist-review.gate.mjs matched the validation-evidence region with a LEFTMOST LAZY regex, so it read ONLY the first evidence block in the plan - which in this plan belongs to the CLOSED Step 14C record - and reported "no specialist review evidence found" for a step that HAD been reviewed. Reproduced deterministically: the old regex window is 700 characters long and contains no APPROVE marker, while the union of all windows does.'
    - 'OBS-N6 (non-blocking, iteration 2): the OBS-F3 scene-stability loop covered only ONE size bucket, so the stability contract was untested for the other bucket.'
    - 'OBS-N7 (non-blocking, iteration 2): a test comment claimed a production constant "does not exist in production yet, so this contract fails today", which was stale - the builder exports that constant since this slice, so the contract is live.'
  resolution:
    - 'OBS-F1: added a full xorshift32 STREAM REPLAY test to right-world.builder.test.ts. The test re-implements the builder PRNG chain as an EXPLICIT ORDERED list - (1) combinedSeed = seed ^ (layoutVersion * 0x9e3779b9); (2) FNV-1a the size-bucket characters onto combinedSeed, one character at a time, as state = Math.imul(state ^ charCode, 16777619), starting from combinedSeed; (3) seed32 = ((combinedSeed >>> 0) ^ 0x72696768) >>> 0; (4) every draw is one xorshift32 step - state ^= state << 13; state ^= state >>> 17; state ^= state << 5; and the draw value is (state >>> 0) / 0x1_0000_0000. It mirrors the per-slot draw order (offset, kind, colour), mirrors the count derivation (requestedCount = min(64, max(1, floor(samples.length / 10))), innerTargetCount = max(1, floor(requestedCount * 0.25)), outerTargetCount = max(1, requestedCount - innerTargetCount)), and asserts the emitted prop list equals the replayed stream prediction AND that the emission ORDER is preserved. FALSIFIABILITY PROVEN: the production line was temporarily mutated to `const kindRoll = index === reservedBleacherSlot ? 0 : random();` (the kind draw SKIPPED at the reserved slot) and the new test FAILED (1 failed / 32 passed) - the probe was then reverted.'

FALSIFIABILITY PROVEN: the production tie-break was temporarily mutated from `gap > bestGap` to `gap >= bestGap` (highest index on a tie) and the test FAILED (1 failed / 32 passed) - the probe was then reverted.'

FALSIFIABILITY PROVEN: resolveRightWorldSeed was temporarily mutated to mix in a module-level call counter, and the new test FAILED (plus 3 more) - the probe was then reverted.'
    - 'OBS-F4: the B5 "Proven remedy" sentence in the plan was reconciled IN PLACE with a dated note pointing at this fix packet, recording WHY the first outer-ring slot cannot be the reserved one (it shares its track station with the first inner-ring slot, and the bleacher 13 m x 9 m footprint then swallows the mechanic/crew pedestal of that same station, hoisting the mechanic billboard onto the bleacher front seat row and breaking the AC-052 mechanic surface contract).'

## PlanUpdate - Step 14N drift-feel integration coupling design (02-researching, read-only)

- `date`: '2026-10-24'
- `step`: '14N'
- `agent`: '02-researching (Tier-1 drift-feel scout)'
- `slice_researched`: 'P1-drift-feel-red (the RED slice that owns the feel direction)'
- `research_artifact`: 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md'
- `files_changed`: 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md (this tracker only) + plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md (new). NO production file was touched.'
- `sub_orchestrators_used`: 'boundary-mapper (drift-yaw ownership chain, tick order, body-matrix composition) and implementation-pattern-scout (test/fixture contract inventory). Both read-only, both re-verified by the orchestrator against the source before anything was written down.'
- `pre_execute_hook`: 'neataptic-workflow-mcp-get_slice_context with slice_id P1-drift-feel-red was invoked as declared by the Step 14N packet.'

### The design model (the answer to the Step 14N research question)

> **The transient drift-yaw accumulator is a TRANSIENT GAIN modulation, and the drift-yaw offset stays exactly proportional to the slip angle:**
>
> ```
> driftYawOffset = slipAngle * (NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD + transientGain)
> ```
>
> The accumulator is a separate, bounded, dimensionless state advanced by a PURE step function in `examples/neatRacing/physics/drift.model.ts`, carried on `PhysicsCarState` (NOT on `DriftModelState`), stepped inside `physics.step.service.ts` after the drift model has produced `slipAngle` and before the offset is computed. It feeds the SINGLE existing `driftYawOffset` scalar, so `car.pass.ts` and `browser-entry.ts` are untouched.

Why this shape (the decisive reasons):

- **Zero straight-line yaw becomes EXACT by construction** - with `slipAngle === 0` the offset is `0` whatever the accumulator holds. An ADDITIVE yaw accumulator would carry a stale yaw onto the next straight line and would need a hard-reset contract. The additive alternative is documented in the research artifact and is NOT recommended (it also has a mid-range NULL where the body lands exactly on the travel direction and the proxy collapses to 0 for a frame or two, which resets the 3-consecutive-frame drift gate).
- **The AC-078 0.002 rad pin is provably invariant.** `tireYawFollowsBodyDuringDrift` measures `wheelYaw - bodyYaw` against `mount.rotationYawRad`, and the wheels are PARENTED onto the body matrix (`car.pass.ts:1598`), so the residual is independent of the offset magnitude. Enlarging the drift cannot move it.
- **`proportionalTractionLoss` is untouched.** The accumulator is VISUAL-ONLY: it never alters `x`, `y`, `heading`, `speed`, `slipAngle` or `lateralVelocity`, so the trajectory stays byte-identical and the 290 km/h ceiling (AC-079) cannot regress.
- **`car.pass.test.ts` stays green.** `DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_LIMIT_RAD` is DERIVED as `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD * NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD`, so it re-derives itself when the base gain moves, and the monotonicity sweep constrains the PASS, not the physics.

### DECISIVE finding 1 - the drift proxy is a V-SHAPED function of the visual gain, with a NULL at 1.0

The fixture measures the proxy from the RENDERED BODY MATRIX against the world-XZ travel chord (`docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html:789-822`), and the physics translates along `heading + slipAngle`. Therefore

```
proxy = |bodyYaw - travelDirection| = |slipAngle| * |GAIN_eff - 1|
```

The recorded baseline `0.049388550574608114 rad` is EXACTLY `0.5 x |slip|` with `|slip| = 0.098777101149216228 rad`, which confirms the identity to the last digit. Consequences the RED slice must internalise BEFORE pinning the floor:

- `GAIN_eff = 0.75` -> proxy 0.0247 (SLIDE SHRINKS); `GAIN_eff = 1.00` -> proxy **0.0000 - THE SLIDE VANISHES**; `GAIN_eff = 1.50` -> 0.0494 (equals today); `GAIN_eff = 2.00` -> 0.0988.
- A naive "raise the gain to feel more drift" move toward 1.0 makes the slide WEAKER while the offset magnitude looks BIGGER. The RED slice must record the `GAIN_eff = +1.0` NULL as a FORBIDDEN region, and is recommended to drive `GAIN_eff` DOWN (monotone, null-free) rather than up.
- The current `GAIN = 0.5` means the body yaw sits at only HALF the physical slip - the "mushy" read the user reported.

### DECISIVE finding 2 - AC-088's named lever CANNOT close the measured residual (plan-level correction required)

`analyzeWheelShading()` (fixture `:605-624`) reads the wheel VBO and averages `max(r,g,b)` of the VERTEX ALBEDO, split by local Y. The mesh builder states it outright (`car.pass.ts:555-556`): *"Vertex colors stay uniform rubber."* - the OBS-20 tire gradient is a FRAGMENT-stage effect (`car.pass.ts:320-329`, uniforms `uTireGradientRadius` / `uTireGradientBrightFactor` / `uTireGradientDarkFactor`) that this measurement path NEVER observes. The mesh is top/bottom symmetric, so `upperAvg === lowerAvg === 0.28565` and the measured gradient is identically zero - and INVARIANT to all three named AC-088 levers.

⇒ **A RED contract of the form "the current fixture's measured gradient is strictly non-zero" is UNSATISFIABLE by tuning the named constants and would strand the tune slice.** The AC-088 lever must be re-scoped to the MEASUREMENT (sample the shaded framebuffer) or the contract must move to its existing jest owner, `examples/neatRacing/engine/lighting.test.ts` (`describe('fixed-space tire lighting (OBS-20)')`). The Step 14N RED packet currently names `examples/neatRacing/engine/passes/car.pass.test.ts` as the tire-gradient file - that is the WRONG owner and the RED slice must correct the file list.

### RED contracts the slice must author (recommended)

1. The AC-087 floor `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SLIDE_PROXY_RAD`, pinned against the measured baseline `0.049388550574608114 rad`, with the recorded feel DIRECTION (bigger slide vs crisper recovery) and the chosen named lever, plus the forbidden `GAIN_eff = +1.0` null.
2. **ZERO STRAIGHT-LINE BODY YAW - a NEW contract.** No assertion anywhere in the repo covers it today (`physics.step.service.test.ts:247-252` pins `speed === MAX` and `slipAngle === 0` but asserts NOTHING about yaw). Under the recommended model it is exact by construction; the contract must exist to keep it that way.
3. A drift-exit reset / recovery contract bound to the recorded decay constant.
4. A regression guard that the 3-consecutive-frame drift gate is never reset by the transient (a single frame below `DRIFT_PROXY_MIN_RAD = 0.01` resets `driftProxyRunFrames` and can break AC-078 AND AC-079 together).
5. The AC-088 measurement/owner correction above.

### Constants that move

- `NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD` (`drift.model.ts:97`, today `0.5`) - the base gain / magnitude lever, with the V-shaped proxy relation and the `+1.0` null.
- NEW in `drift.model.ts`: `NEATRACING_DRIFT_TRANSIENT_GAIN_MAX` (must be chosen so `|GAIN_eff| * |slipAngle| < PI/2`, the `physics.step.service.test.ts:162` pin), `NEATRACING_DRIFT_TRANSIENT_GAIN_RATE_PER_S` (build) and `NEATRACING_DRIFT_TRANSIENT_GAIN_DECAY_PER_S` (recovery - THESE TWO TRADE OFF, and that trade-off IS the feel decision), and `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SLIDE_PROXY_RAD` (the AC-087 floor; the browser fixture hardcodes its own constants, so the floor needs a single source of truth AND a mirrored literal).
- CANDIDATE in `car.pass.ts`: `NEATRACING_TIRE_GRADIENT_RADIUS_M`, decoupling `uTireGradientRadius` from `NEATRACING_WHEEL_HUB_HEIGHT_M` (today `car.pass.ts:1469` feeds the wheel-MOUNT constant into the lighting uniform) - correct hygiene, but per DECISIVE finding 2 it CANNOT by itself close the measured residual.
- MUST NOT MOVE (physics constants - they change the trajectory and would break AC-079/AC-089): `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SPEED_MPS`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_THRESHOLD_RAD`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_RATE_PER_RAD`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_LONGITUDINAL_TRACTION_LOSS_RATE_PER_S`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_RECOVERY_RATE_PER_S`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_LATERAL_GRIP_RATE_PER_S`, `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD`.

### State ownership and tick order (recorded)

- `PhysicsCarState` (`physics.step.service.ts:73-112`) owns the new numeric field; the session (`host/race-session.ts:81-89`) replaces the record wholesale each tick, so the field must be carried forward. There is NO worker / postMessage boundary today (main thread only), so no clone/transfer concerns.
- `DriftModelState` has exactly TWO fields and is byte-identity pinned by AC-047D (`drift.model.test.ts:309-327`), so the accumulator is a SEPARATE type in `drift.model.ts` and is NOT a `DriftModelState` field.
- Tick order: rAF -> `handleFrame` -> 0..4 fixed ticks of 1/60 s -> per tick `stepPhysics` then `stepRaceRules` -> `hud.update` -> `composer.drawFrame` -> `browser-entry.ts:941` -> `carPass.draw`. The accumulator is stepped in TICK order (after the drift model produced `slipAngle`, before the offset is computed); the body matrix is built ONCE per rendered frame from the last tick's offset, exactly as today.
- The determinism test compares run A vs run B of the SAME code (never a golden literal), so adding a field to `PhysicsCarState` is safe.

### Blockers / open items owned by the RED slice

- The feel DIRECTION (bigger slide vs crisper recovery) and the floor VALUE are NOT invented here - they are the RED slice's explicit decision per the Step 14N amendment note.
- The slip envelope at the pinned `physics.step.service.test.ts` fixture is not yet measured, so `NEATRACING_DRIFT_TRANSIENT_GAIN_MAX` cannot be bounded yet.
- AC-088 needs a plan-level lever correction (measurement) and a file-owner correction (`engine/lighting.test.ts`, not `car.pass.test.ts`).

### Carried-forward residuals (recorded, not owned by Step 14N)

- `examples/neatRacing/engine/passes/glass.pass.ts:1048,1086` reads `car.yawRad` / `steerAngleRad` but NOT `driftYawOffsetRad` - the glass canopy stays on base yaw while the body yaws; feel work AMPLIFIES this visible mismatch.
- `examples/neatRacing/physics/collision.utils.ts:410,417-418` zeroes `speed` / `slipAngle` / `lateralVelocity` on a bounce but NOT `driftYawOffset` - dormant today, latent once the accumulator is wired (the recommended slip-proportional model makes it self-healing).
- Spec drift is already live: the spec's illustrative formula is `clamp(lateralVelocity/speed * GAIN, +-max)` while the implementation is `atan2(...) * GAIN` with NO clamp.
- `drift.model.ts:363` `computeDriftYawOffset()` is a DEAD export (production inlines the multiplication) - a cleanup candidate, not a Step 14N action.
- **WORKFLOW TOOLING GAP (pre-existing, NOT introduced by this research pass):** `.github/hooks/workflow-update-sync.mjs` parses step headings with `/^#{4,5}\s+(?:Step|Packet)\s+([A-Z]?\d+)\s+(?:—|-)\s+(.+)\s\[([A-Z]+)\]/`. That id pattern accepts `14` and `E1`-style ids but NOT a letter-SUFFIXED id, so the heading `#### Step 14N - ... [WIP]` is never parsed as a step entry. The hook therefore reports `currentWipStep: null` / `actionTaken: 'between-steps'` even though Step 14N IS `[WIP]`, and it will NOT auto-advance Step 14N -> Step 15. The hook still returns `ok: true` / `pass: true` and the `plan-sync` gate still passes, so this is a silent degradation, not a failure. The step advancement must be driven MANUALLY by the orchestrator. Owner: the workflow-hook maintainer (`.github/hooks/`), which is OUTSIDE this research slice's edit scope.

### DECISIVE FINDINGS (arcade-refs)

- **The user verdict is CORRECT, and stronger than stated: the current drift model is not merely "slow" - the countersteer CANNOT catch the slide, it MIRRORS it.** Reproduced the model's equations and simulated them at 60 Hz:
  - **25 m/s (the fixture's 90 km/h operating point), full left steer:** the slip plateaus at **-4.50 deg** (proxy 0.0392 rad) - too small to read, and it takes ~0.25 s / ~0.75 s to reach 63 % / 95 % of that. **This is the "tilt too slow / icy" complaint.**
  - **89 m/s, full left steer:** the slip reaches **-65.8 deg AND KEEPS GROWING**; the effective damping collapses **4.0/s -> 0.51/s** as the slip grows (more slip => less traction => less damping => more slip). **Positive feedback, not a grip budget.**
  - **Full COUNTERSTEER:** 25 m/s -> the slip crosses zero and **parks at +4.48 deg**, a mirror-image equilibrium of the same size; 89 m/s -> **-65.8 deg becomes +52.2 deg** and never recovers. **The countersteer inverts the car.**
  - **Root cause (verified in source, two independent parts):** (1) the "centrifugal" outward push is a function of the YAW RATE, and the yaw rate is a function of the STEER - so countersteering REVERSES the push and the two terms ADD instead of opposing; (2) the countersteer gate `steer * sign(slip) > 0` **closes the instant the slip crosses zero**, switching off the very authority that could catch the slide. Plus the countersteer magnitude is tiny: 12/s x speedPercent = 3.4 m/s^2 at 25 m/s vs the push's 8.4 m/s^2.
  - **=> "Bounce-back must be sharper" is a MISSING-AUTHORITY / WRONG-GATE problem, not a rate problem. Raising `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_RECOVERY_RATE_PER_S` (the code-map scout's lever #5) would make the inversion FASTER and HARDER, not better.**
- **C1 (verified):** the production `NEATRACING_PHYSICS_CENTRIFUGAL_MULTIPLIER` is **1.5** (`physics.step.service.ts:184`), NOT the 0.3 that `drift.model.ts:119` claims in its JSDoc. The JSDoc is wrong and every feel number derived from it is wrong.
- **C6:** `outwardPush` is dimensionally inconsistent - `yawRatePerTick` is radians PER TICK, so `rad/tick x m/s` is not m/s. The correct centripetal term is `yawRate[rad/s] x speed[m/s] x dt`.
- **C7:** `0.6 x |slip| x speed x speedPercent` = **24.2 m/s^2** at 26 deg / 89 m/s, i.e. **larger than the engine's 17.8 m/s^2**. The car cannot hold speed in a deep slide.
- **Proxy identity (confirmed to the last digit, and independently by both repo scouts):** `proxy = |slip| x |GAIN - 1|`, so the recorded **0.049388550574608114 rad** baseline implies `|slip| ~ 0.0988 rad = 5.66 deg`. **The proxy is V-shaped in the gain with a NULL at GAIN = 1.0** - raising the gain makes the slide WEAKER. The only monotone direction is DOWN.

### THE MODEL (stated explicitly, as the charter requires)

- Seven stages, all in `drift.model.ts`: (0) drift latch - `turnSign` latched at entry; (1) committed drift angle - rate-limited ramp IN (`ENTRY_RATE_RAD_PER_S`), linear unwind OUT (`EXIT_RATE_RAD_PER_S`), clamped to `+-MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD`; (2) tire saturation as a BUDGET `gripFactor = 1/(1 + RATE x max(0,|slip| - THRESHOLD))`; (3) physical chase `vLat += (tan(committed) x speed - vLat) x (1 - exp(-dt x gripFactor / TAU))`; (4) **countersteer authority applied AGAINST the slide** `vLat += turnSign x COUNTERSTEER_AUTHORITY_MPS x |steer| x speedPercent x dt`; (5) hard zero `if (!drifting && |slip| < SNAP_BACK_ZERO) { vLat = 0; committed = 0; }`; (6) saturating speed scrub; (7) **visible pose as a SECOND-ORDER spring-damper** `poseTarget = slip x GAIN + POSE_STEER_YAW_RAD x steer x speedPercent x min(1, |slip|/FULL_SLIP_RAD)`.
- **Sign convention pinned to production (verified):** `lateralVelocity > 0` = the velocity lies LEFT of the heading, so a LEFT turn produces a NEGATIVE slip and the visible offset `slip x GAIN` is negative. **The upstream research draft's `-committed` in the pose target is a SIGN ERROR under this convention and would mirror the whole drift - the implementer must use the corrected form in the research artifact D1.**

### THE CONSTANT SET (for `drift.model.ts`)

- `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD = 0.45` (25.8 deg; was `Math.PI/2` - and note it is UNUSED inside its own module, so it is an envelope pin, not a lever) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SPEED_MPS = 15` (unchanged) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_ENTRY_RATE_RAD_PER_S = 3.5` (201 deg/s) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_EXIT_RATE_RAD_PER_S = 2.0` (115 deg/s) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_SLIP_RESPONSE_TAU_S = 0.045` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_THRESHOLD_RAD = 0.20` (was 0.25) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_GRIP_FALLOFF_RATE_PER_RAD = 2` (unchanged) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_AUTHORITY_MPS = 70` (m/s^2) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_MIN_SLIP_RAD = 0.02` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_SNAP_BACK_ZERO_SLIP_RAD = 0.02` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STIFFNESS_RAD_PER_S2 = 324` (omega = 18 rad/s, f = 2.86 Hz) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_DAMPING_RAD_PER_S = 12.6` (zeta = 0.35 => 31 % first overshoot) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STEER_YAW_RAD = 0.08` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STEER_YAW_FULL_SLIP_RAD = 0.10` · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_SPEED_SCRUB_COEFF_PER_S = 0.25` (was 0.6) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD = 0.5` (UNCHANGED - it stays the base gain).
- **Retired by this model:** `NEATRACING_DRIFT_LATERAL_GRIP_RATE_PER_S` (4) -> `SLIP_RESPONSE_TAU_S` + the saturation budget; `NEATRACING_DRIFT_COUNTERSTEER_RECOVERY_RATE_PER_S` (12) -> `COUNTERSTEER_AUTHORITY_MPS`; `NEATRACING_DRIFT_LONGITUDINAL_TRACTION_LOSS_RATE_PER_S` (0.6) -> `SPEED_SCRUB_COEFF_PER_S` (0.25, saturating rather than proportional-to-speed).

### MERGE RECOMMENDATION (criterion: fun / exciting)

- **The already-recorded coupling design's "Track A" (visual-only transient gain) is a strict SUBSET of this model.** The coupling design's transient gain and this model's pose spring-damper are the SAME mechanism (a second-order visual channel); this model just sources it from the physical slip instead of a synthetic gain, so the visual swing and the physical catch become one coherent thing.
- **Track A alone CANNOT satisfy the user verdict.** The operative clause is *"bounce-back must be sharper"* and the bounce-back is PHYSICAL. A cosmetic swing on a car that is still sliding the wrong way is not a fix. If the budget cannot absorb the re-baselining, Track A is a reasonable INTERIM (drive the gain DOWN: proxy `0.0988 x 1.5 = 0.148 rad` = 3.0x baseline, byte-identical trajectory) but it must be recorded as **cosmetic-only**.
- **RECOMMENDED MIX: (1) the physical model as a NEW slice with re-baselining; (2) the pose spring-damper as the visual half of it; (3) the AC-087 floor re-pinned on the DETERMINISTIC unit proxy, not the noisy browser proxy (recorded spread 0.0494 / 0.0603 / 0.3599 rad - a floor pinned to 0.0494 would sit inside the noise band).**

- `scout`: 'game-feel' (a FRESH re-dispatch of the cancelled agent d55cf63f) — charter: *"spring-damper response design - attack rates, damping ratio, overshoot, anticipation - concrete accumulator params for arcade drift feel"*.
- `status`: 'SUCCESS (research complete; no production change; no file in src/ or examples/ touched)'.
- `research_artifact`: 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.drift-feel.research.md' — sections **E6** (evidence) and **D6** (decision) are the game-feel addendum; E1-E5 / D1-D5 (the arcade-refs brief) are UNCHANGED. The PRIMARY Step 14N artifact remains 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.research.md' (the coupling design) — **also unchanged**.
- `sub_orchestrators_used`: 'implementation-pattern-scout' (repo Tier-3) and 'boundary-mapper' (repo Tier-3) — both dispatched with `build_dispatch_packet` packets that returned `ok:true, dispatch_allowed:true`.
- `model`: '**THE ARCADE-REFS SPRING IS ALREADY RIGHT — do NOT re-tune it. The single defect is the DISCONTINUOUS pose TARGET (the raw-steer articulation term). Replace that term with a SLEW-LIMITED articulation and the far-side pop is PRESERVED while the body twitch is removed. The asymmetric-damping "fix" for the entry overshoot is REFUTED by measurement: it destroys the pop.**'
- `method`: 'I reproduced the arcade-refs 7-stage model at 60 Hz in a scratch harness (`tmp/driftfeel-final.mjs`, gitignored) and VALIDATED the harness against the artifact\'s own published D3 numbers before trusting anything: entry overshoot 17.6 %, catch dive -3.67 deg, far-side pop +2.61 deg, settle 550 ms, max target step -4.65 deg, peak pose rate 108 deg/s — all matched to the digit. Every figure below is machine-produced by that harness.'

### DECISIVE FINDINGS (game-feel)

- **GF-1 (0.97) — THE ARCADE-REFS SPRING CONSTANTS ARE CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE RE-TUNED.** The obvious reading of the entry overshoot is "the body wobbles into the slide, so damp the attack harder". **Measurement refutes it.** Replacing the arcade-refs' SYMMETRIC `zeta = 0.35` with an asymmetric rule (`zeta_attack = 0.9` on the attack, `zeta_release = 0.35` on the release) collapses the far-side pop from **2.61 deg to 0.00 deg** (measured at both omega = 18 and omega = 24). **=> THE ENTRY OVERSHOOT IS NOT A DEFECT: IT IS THE ENERGY RESERVOIR THAT PRODUCES THE POP.** The symmetric `zeta = 0.35` spring IS the pop's engine. The entry overshoot is **1.79 deg absolute** (17.6 % of the 10.16 deg hold target) — the body settles ~1.8 deg into the slide and rings down over ~350 ms. That is the "settle into the slide" an arcade drifter needs. **`NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STIFFNESS_RAD_PER_S2 = 324` (omega = 18 rad/s, 2.86 Hz) and `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_DAMPING_RAD_PER_S = 12.6` (zeta = 0.35) STAY EXACTLY AS THE ARCADE-REFS SCOUT SET THEM.**
- **GF-2 (0.95) — THE SINGLE REAL DEFECT IS THE POSE TARGET'S DISCONTINUITY, NOT THE SPRING.** The arcade-refs stage 7 target is `poseTarget = slip x GAIN + 0.08 x steer x speedPercent x min(1, |slip|/0.10)`. The steer term flips sign on every countersteer, so the target **STEPS by `2 x 0.08 x speedPercent`**: **1.83 deg at 20 % speed, 5.13 deg at 56 % (the measured hold point), 9.17 deg at 89 m/s.** A second-order system converts a target step into a velocity impulse, so the kick's size is a function of the **STEP SIZE, not of zeta**. **=> "the bounce-back must be sharper" is NOT deliverable by tuning the arcade-refs' spring.** The step also fires on every steer sign change (twitchy) and grows with speed.
- **GF-3 (0.93) — BUT THE POP IS NOT THE STEP.** Removing the discontinuity (slew-limited articulation) leaves the far-side pop at **2.22-2.30 deg** vs the arcade's 2.61 deg — the step contributes only ~0.3-0.4 deg of the pop and ~0.7 deg of the outward dive. **=> The discontinuity is a TWITCH defect, not the pop's energy source.** Separating the two is the crux: the pop must be KEPT, the step must go.
- **GF-4 (0.92) — THE CONCRETE ACCUMULATOR: A SLEW-LIMITED ARTICULATION.** Replace the raw steer term with a single rate-limited articulation state, with the slip gate INSIDE the slew's target so that no term can ever step:

  ```
  artTarget  = steer x speedPercent x min(1, |slip| / ARM_SLIP_RAD)
  art       += clamp(artTarget - art, -ARTICULATION_SLEW_PER_S x dt, +ARTICULATION_SLEW_PER_S x dt)
  poseTarget  = slip x VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD + ARTICULATION_RAD x art
  poseRate   += (STIFFNESS x (poseTarget - pose) - DAMPING x poseRate) x dt
  pose       += poseRate x dt
  ```

  **Provable per-tick bound: `max |d(poseTarget)| <= ARTICULATION_RAD x ARTICULATION_SLEW_PER_S x dt + 0.5 x |slip_at_hard_zero|`.** The bound is **speed-independent** (the raw term's is proportional to `speedPercent`). Measured: **2.13 deg/tick at slew = 20 /s vs the arcade's 4.65 deg/tick at 50 m/s and 9.17 deg/tick at 89 m/s.**
- **GF-5 (0.92) — THE ANTICIPATION MUST BE A PROPERTY OF THE TARGET, AND THE ARCADE-REFS' GATE DEFEATS IT.** With the new `ENTRY_RATE 3.5 rad/s` the gate `min(1, |slip|/0.10)` is saturated for essentially the whole drift, so the arcade-refs' term is a **raw-steer offset, not a lead** — the anticipation is effectively ABSENT from the arcade-refs model. Lowering the arm threshold to **0.01 rad** (engage on the FIRST tick of the slide) plus the slew's ramp-in (`1/SLEW .. 2/SLEW` = 50-100 ms at 20-30 /s) restores a genuine, continuous lead that precedes the body's commitment. Measured: the arm threshold is free below 0.02 rad (pop 2.22 deg, step 2.13 deg at arm = 0.005 / 0.01 / 0.02 — identical), so arming earlier costs nothing. **=> ARM = 0.01 rad.**
- **GF-6 (0.90) — THE ANTICIPATION LAG AND THE ANTI-TWITCH BOUND ARE THE SAME DIAL; A SLEW IS THE RIGHT TOOL, NOT A TAU LAG.** The house idiom is first-order TAU smoothing, but a TAU lag's per-tick step is `2 x ART x speedPercent x dt/tau` — **speed-dependent and amplitude-dependent** — whereas the slew's is `ART x SLEW x dt` — **speed-independent and amplitude-independent**. The slew therefore keeps the step bound tight while the articulation amplitude (and hence the pop) is free to grow. A TAU lag at the same timing buys a smaller step only by shrinking the articulation, i.e. by shrinking the pop. **=> USE THE SLEW.** (A first-order lag is still a valid fallback if the RED slice prefers the house idiom, at the cost of a speed-dependent step bound — recorded as an open choice, not a recommendation.)
- **GF-7 (0.93) — THE ATTACK RATE IS NOT THE SPRING'S; IT IS THE PHYSICAL SLIP DYNAMICS'.** This is the charter's "attack rate" question, answered: **the onset is IDENTICAL across every variant tested** (raw, tau-filtered, slewed, asymmetric, omega = 12..32): the body reaches **25 % of the hold delta at 33.3 ms and 50 % at 66.7 ms** after the steer input. The spring contributes <= 1-2 ticks of lag; the committed-angle ramp (`ENTRY_RATE 3.5 rad/s`) + the slip chase (`SLIP_RESPONSE_TAU_S 45 ms`) set the attack. **=> THE SPRING's omega IS FREE — it can be raised for a crisper pop without touching the perceived attack. Do NOT spend the accumulator's budget on the attack; spend it on the pop.**
- **GF-8 (0.92) — omega AND zeta ARE THE SAME TRADE-OFF DIAL (pop vs ring-out), AND THE ENVELOPE BOUNDS omega FROM ABOVE.** Measured (slew 20, art 0.08, arm 0.01): `omega=15, zeta=0.35` -> pop 2.62 deg, settle 650 ms; `omega=18, zeta=0.35` -> **pop 2.22 deg, settle 550 ms**; `omega=21, zeta=0.35` -> pop 1.76 deg, settle 383 ms; `omega=24, zeta=0.35` -> pop 1.37 deg, settle 367 ms; `omega=18, zeta=0.25` -> pop 3.40 deg, settle 717 ms; `omega=18, zeta=0.45` -> pop 1.35 deg, settle 433 ms. **The pop and the settle are strictly monotone in BOTH, in opposite directions.** **=> THE RED SLICE MUST PICK ONE (omega, zeta) POINT AND PIN THE POP *AND* THE SETTLE TOGETHER — not just the hold pose.**
- **GF-9 (0.90) — NEW ENVELOPE VIOLATION, NOT IN D3: the arcade-refs' pose spring OVERSHOOTS the declared `DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_LIMIT_RAD` BY 2 %.** The declared envelope is `MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD x VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD = 0.45 x 0.5 = 0.2250 rad (12.89 deg)`. The measured **max |pose| during the arcade-refs' entry overshoot is 13.15 deg = 0.2295 rad — 2.00 % OVER the limit.** The recommended slew-limited variant lands at **12.87 deg = 0.2246 rad (0.19 % inside)**. **=> THE LIMIT MUST BE RE-DERIVED FROM THE MEASURED PEAK, NOT FROM `MAX_SLIP x GAIN`** — and `omega = 18` is not merely the arcade-refs' preference, it is **the largest omega that keeps the pose inside the declared envelope at zeta = 0.35** (`omega = 15` -> max |pose| 13.29 deg = 0.232 rad, 3 % over). **=> THIS IS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT REASON TO KEEP omega = 18.**
- **GF-10 (0.92) — THE SPRING MUST BE STEPPED INSIDE THE 60 Hz `stepPhysics` TICK, NEVER IN THE RENDER PATH.** (boundary-mapper) The drift yaw is written once per 60 Hz tick (`physics.step.service.ts:416-417` -> `:440`), bridged once per render frame (`browser-entry.ts:941`), and read in exactly TWO places (`car.pass.ts:1365` shadow, `:1567` body matrix); the tires inherit it via body-matrix parenting (`:1598`). **There is NO interpolation anywhere**, and the tick:frame ratio is `displayHz/60` (1 @ 60 Hz, 2 @ 144 Hz, 2.75 @ 165 Hz, max 4 catch-up steps/frame). **=> A per-frame spring would run 2.4x faster at 144 Hz than at 60 Hz: the feel would be display-rate dependent and the jest/browser parity would break. The accumulator MUST live on the 60 Hz tick.**
- **GF-11 (0.90) — THE POSE CHANNEL IS THE *ONLY* VISUAL READ OF THE SLIDE.** (boundary-mapper) **The chase camera does NOT consume `driftYawOffsetRad`** (`browser-entry.ts:955` — the camera yaw is trajectory-only). The camera tracks the trajectory while the body slides inside it. **=> THE POSE SPRING CARRIES THE ENTIRE DRIFT FEEL, and the anticipation term is the first thing the player sees.** (And `computeDriftYawOffset` at `drift.model.ts:363` is a DEAD export — wire it up or delete it in the same step; it is the natural home for the new pose state.)
- **GF-12 (0.95) — THERE IS NO SECOND-ORDER PRECEDENT IN THE REPO; THE SPRING IS A DELIBERATE DEPARTURE AND NEEDS A NEW STATE TYPE.** (implementation-pattern-scout) No second-order spring/damper exists anywhere in `src/` or `examples/neatRacing`; the house idiom is FIRST-ORDER TAU smoothing (`editor.camera.ts:48-56,430-447`; `NEATRACING_EDITOR_CAMERA_SMOOTHING_TAU_S = 0.08`). A first-order filter cannot overshoot, so the spring is not an idiom question but a corpus question (the SMK/MKWii "pose-vs-velocity split" the arcade-refs brief cites). **The state must be a NEW SEPARATE type — `DriftPoseSpringState { pose; poseRate; articulation }` + `createZeroDriftPoseSpringState()` + `stepDriftPoseSpring(prev, input)` — carried on `PhysicsCarState` (which IS safe to extend) and NOT on `DriftModelState` (byte-identity pinned, AC-047D).** The slew adds a THIRD scalar, so the state is three scalars, not two.
- **GF-13 (0.95) — THE ZERO-STRAIGHT-LINE-YAW GUARANTEE IS EXACT, AND IS A FREE RED CONTRACT.** Measured over a 5 s run with no steering input: **max |pose| = 0.000000000 rad, max |poseTarget| = 0.000000000 rad, max per-tick step = 0.000000 deg, final pose = 0.000000000 rad.** The residual pose after a settled drift is **-0.000 deg** (the arcade-refs' slip-gated term preserves it). **=> THE RED CONTRACT SHOULD PIN THIS AS AN EXACT IDENTITY (to 1e-9), NOT A TOLERANCE.**
- **GF-14 (0.95) — STABILITY: NO SUB-STEPPING IS REQUIRED, AND THE ACCUMULATOR IS DETERMINISTIC.** At `dt = 1/60` with semi-implicit Euler: `omega = 18` -> `omega x dt = 0.300`, `C x dt = 0.210`, `K x dt^2 = 0.090`; `omega = 24` -> 0.400 / 0.280 / 0.160; `omega = 32` -> 0.533 / 0.373 / 0.284. All are well under 2, so the spring is unconditionally stable at 60 Hz. The unit-step response at the arcade-refs' point is: **t63 = 50.0 ms, t95 = 83.3 ms, first overshoot 29.06 %, peak at 150 ms, settle-after-t95 450 ms.**
- **GF-15 (0.85) — STRESS, FLAGGED NOT FIXED: STEER CHATTER.** A 4 Hz square-wave steer on the committed-drift model drives the far-side body swing to **22.6 deg** (556 % of the hold delta) and the settle to ~2 s. The slew-limited articulation bounds the per-tick target step but does NOT by itself suppress the committed model's chatter response — **this is a property of the arcade-refs' LATCH design, not of the pose channel, and it is OUT of the game-feel charter's scope. It is raised to Phase B as a risk on the latch.**
- **GF-16 (0.90) — THE POP IS NOT AN ARTEFACT OF A FULL COUNTERSTEER.** With a partial countersteer (-0.4 steer) the recommended variant still produces a **1.92 deg** far-side pop with a -1.88 deg dive, a 1.89 deg max step and a 533 ms settle — the pop scales with the countersteer authority, so it is a coherent response, not a full-input artefact. (A short flick with the steer released leaves a sustained committed drift, so the pose does not return to zero — that is the arcade-refs' latch behaviour, out of this charter's scope.)

### THE CONSTANT SET (the concrete accumulator params)

- **UNCHANGED from the arcade-refs (do not re-tune):** `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STIFFNESS_RAD_PER_S2 = 324` (omega = 18 rad/s = 2.86 Hz) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_DAMPING_RAD_PER_S = 12.6` (zeta = 0.35) · `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STEER_YAW_RAD = 0.08` (the articulation amplitude; keep the arcade-refs' name or rename to `..._ARTICULATION_RAD` — an implementation-naming decision for the RED slice).
- **CHANGED:** `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_STEER_YAW_FULL_SLIP_RAD` (the arm threshold) **0.10 -> 0.01** (arm the anticipation on the FIRST tick; free below 0.02 rad).
- **NEW:** `NEATRACING_DRIFT_POSE_ARTICULATION_SLEW_PER_S` — **band 15-30 /s, 20 /s recommended.** Measured at omega = 18, zeta = 0.35, art 0.08, arm 0.01: slew 10 -> pop 1.82 deg / step 1.47 deg; slew 15 -> 2.10 / 1.75; **slew 20 -> 2.22 / 2.13**; slew 30 -> 2.30 / 2.89; slew 45 -> 2.34 / 3.37; slew 60 -> 2.33 / 4.06. The **settle is invariant at 550 ms across the whole band** (the ring-out is the spring's, not the articulation's) and the pop saturates at slew >= 30. **The in-band choice is the RED slice (`P1-drift-feel-red`) DECISION, not this scout's.**
- **NEW (state):** `DriftPoseSpringState { pose; poseRate; articulation }` on `PhysicsCarState`, with `createInitialPhysicsCarState` initialising all three to 0 and `stepPhysics` carrying them into the returned record.
- **NAMING / GRAMMAR (house rules):** `NEATRACING_<DOMAIN>_<SUBJECT>_<UNIT>`; unit suffixes `_RAD`, `_MPS`, `_PER_S`, `_PER_S2`; floor/ceiling infixes `MIN_`/`MAX_`; one `export const` block at the top of the file.

### PLAN CORRECTIONS THIS SCOUT REQUIRES

1. **RECORD THE ASYMMETRIC-DAMPING IDEA AS REFUTED** so no Phase-B agent re-derives it: measured, it collapses the far-side pop from 2.61 deg to 0.00 deg. The symmetric `zeta = 0.35` spring is the pop's engine and the entry overshoot is its energy reservoir.
2. **AMEND the arcade-refs D1 stage 7 (the pose target) and D2 (two constants)** — the arcade-refs model is otherwise UNCHANGED. This is an amendment, not a replacement: the committed-drift model, the grip budget, the countersteer authority and the hard zero all stand.
3. **MERGE THE TWO VISUAL CHANNELS INTO ONE ACCUMULATOR.** The coupling design's `DriftTransientGainState` (2 scalars) and the arcade-refs' pose spring (2 scalars) are the SAME mechanism. With the slew the pose state is **THREE** scalars. **Phase B must ship ONE `DriftPoseSpringState` on `PhysicsCarState`, not two competing accumulators.** This merge conflict is the main reason this scout exists.
4. **THE RED SLICE MUST PIN THREE NUMBERS, NOT ONE:** the far-side pop, the settle time, and the max per-tick pose-TARGET step — all at one `(omega, zeta, art, arm, slew)` point. Pinning only the hold pose would let a future edit silently destroy the pop.
5. **THE RED SLICE MUST PIN THE ZERO-STRAIGHT-LINE-YAW GUARANTEE AS AN EXACT IDENTITY** (to 1e-9) — it is exact today and is the cheapest possible regression guard.
6. **RE-DERIVE `DRIFT_VISUAL_YAW_LIMIT_RAD` FROM THE MEASURED PEAK, NOT FROM `MAX_SLIP x GAIN`.** The declared 0.2250 rad is exceeded by 2.00 % by the arcade-refs' own entry overshoot. Either the limit moves to the measured peak (0.2295 rad) or the pose stays inside it (the recommended variant, 0.2246 rad). The existing pin at `physics.step.service.test.ts:156-163` (`|driftYawOffset| < Math.PI/2` and `spawn.driftYawOffset === 0`) must be re-verified against the overshoot.
7. **THE POP IS A CORPUS REQUIREMENT, SO IT MUST BE A NAMED CONTRACT, NOT AN INCIDENTAL OUTCOME.** The arcade-refs brief cites the SMK/MKWii "pose-vs-velocity split"; a future "tidy-up" that raises `zeta` to 0.45 (or `omega` to 24) silently halves the pop. Pin it in the RED slice with a stated minimum.

### GAPS (flagged, not invented)

- **No published arcade racing game states a spring-damper constant set for the VISUAL pose channel.** The values here are derived, not transcribed. The corpus (the arcade-refs brief) supplies the *behavioural* requirements (a visible pop, a held slide, a sharp catch), not the numbers.
- **The 4 Hz steer-chatter stress (GF-15) was NOT reproduced against production** — it is a model-level observation on my reproduction of the arcade-refs model, and it is raised as a risk, not a defect claim.
- **The pop's perceptual threshold is not measured.** 15 % of the hold delta (2.22 deg) is asserted to be "felt" from the corpus's qualitative description of the SMK/MKWii snap, not from a psychophysical measurement. **The RED slice and the browser smoke fixture are where that judgement must be made.**
- **I did not test the pose channel against the CANOPY mismatch** (`glass.pass.ts:1048,1086` never reads `driftYawOffsetRad`, so a bigger slide amplifies the body-vs-canopy mismatch). Carried forward from the arcade-refs report; a bigger pop makes it worse, and it is not fixable inside the pose channel.
- **`collision.utils.ts:410,417-418`** zeroes speed/slip/lateralVelocity on a bounce but NOT `driftYawOffset` — latent once the accumulator is wired. Unchanged by this scout; the pose state must be reset there too.

### CERTAINTY

- **0.97** on GF-1 (the symmetric `zeta = 0.35` spring is the pop's engine; the asymmetric-damping fix is refuted) — measured, and the harness is validated against the artifact's own D3 numbers to the digit.
- **0.95** on GF-2 / GF-3 (the target's discontinuity is the real defect; the pop is not the step) — measured, with the step-vs-pop separation isolated.
- **0.95** on GF-12 / GF-13 / GF-14 (no second-order precedent; the exact zero-straight-line identity; the stability margins) — source read + measurement.
- **0.93** on GF-4 / GF-5 (the slew-limited articulation and the arm threshold) — measured, with the per-tick bound derived.
- **0.92** on GF-7 / GF-8 / GF-9 / GF-10 / GF-11 / GF-16 — measured (GF-7, GF-8, GF-9, GF-16) and source-verified (GF-10, GF-11).
- **0.90** on GF-6 (slew over TAU) and on the constant set. **The choice INSIDE each band is a RED-slice decision, not this scout's.**
- **0.85** on GF-15 (the chatter stress) — a model-level observation, deliberately reported as a risk.
- **0.80** on the merge recommendation (a judgement about plan shape, not a measurement).

### THE SELECTED MIX (the design Phase B must plan and RED must pin)

1. **PHYSICAL HALF - the arcade-refs 7-stage committed-drift model, ADOPTED.** The root cause is PHYSICAL (the countersteer mirrors the slide: the centrifugal push is yaw-rate-driven so countersteer REVERSES it, and the gate `steer*sign(slip)>0` closes at zero-slip crossing; authority 3.4 vs push 8.4 m/s^2), so "bounce-back must be sharper" is NOT deliverable by visual tuning alone. Track A (visual-only transient gain) is REJECTED as the primary fix - cosmetic interim only, and the budget no longer requires an interim.
2. **VISUAL HALF - ONE merged accumulator: `DriftPoseSpringState { pose; poseRate; articulation }` (THREE scalars) on `PhysicsCarState`.** The coupling design's DriftTransientGainState and the arcade-refs' pose spring are the SAME mechanism - they MUST NOT ship as two competing accumulators. NOT on DriftModelState (AC-047D byte-pin). Spring constants STAY as arcade-refs set them: STIFFNESS 324 (omega=18) / DAMPING 12.6 (zeta=0.35) - the symmetric spring IS the pop's engine; asymmetric damping is REFUTED by measurement (collapses the far-side pop 2.61 -> 0.00 deg).
3. **THE GAME-FEEL AMENDMENT - slew-limited articulation replaces the raw-steer pose term:** `artTarget = steer x speedPercent x min(1, |slip|/ARM)`; `art += clamp(artTarget - art, +-SLEW x dt)`; `poseTarget = slip x GAIN + ARTICULATION_RAD x art`; `poseRate += (STIFFNESS x (poseTarget - pose) - DAMPING x poseRate) x dt`; `pose += poseRate x dt`. ARM 0.10 -> **0.01 rad**; SLEW band 15-30/s, **20 recommended** (RED decides in-band; settle invariant 550 ms across the band). Preserves the pop (2.22 deg), kills the twitch (max per-tick target step 4.65-9.17 deg -> 2.13 deg, SPEED-INDEPENDENT), fixes the 2.00 % envelope violation (max |pose| 0.2246 rad, inside the 0.2250 limit).
4. **CONSTANT SET (single source, drift.model.ts):** MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD 0.45 / MIN_SPEED_MPS 15 / ENTRY_RATE_RAD_PER_S 3.5 / EXIT_RATE_RAD_PER_S 2.0 / SLIP_RESPONSE_TAU_S 0.045 / GRIP_FALLOFF_THRESHOLD_RAD 0.20 / GRIP_FALLOFF_RATE_PER_RAD 2 / COUNTERSTEER_AUTHORITY_MPS 70 / COUNTERSTEER_MIN_SLIP_RAD 0.02 / SNAP_BACK_ZERO_SLIP_RAD 0.02 / POSE_STIFFNESS_RAD_PER_S2 324 / POSE_DAMPING_RAD_PER_S 12.6 / POSE_STEER_YAW_RAD 0.08 / POSE_STEER_YAW_FULL_SLIP_RAD 0.01 / NEW POSE_ARTICULATION_SLEW_PER_S 20 (band 15-30) / SPEED_SCRUB_COEFF_PER_S 0.25 / VISUAL_YAW_GAIN_RAD 0.5 unchanged. RETIRES: LATERAL_GRIP_RATE_PER_S, COUNTERSTEER_RECOVERY_RATE_PER_S, LONGITUDINAL_TRACTION_LOSS_RATE_PER_S.
5. **MUST-NOT-MOVE PIN: LIFTED for this slice.** The model replacement changes the trajectory BY DESIGN; AC-079 (290 km/h ceiling) and AC-089 are RE-BASELINED, not preserved. Phase B must produce the re-baselining plan (the ceiling was most at risk per the code-map fixture-risk map).
6. **SIGN CONVENTION:** LEFT turn = negative slip (pinned to production). The upstream research draft's `-committed` in the pose target is a SIGN ERROR under this convention - use the corrected form (research artifact D1).
7. **RED CONTRACTS Phase B must specify:** (a) far-side pop floor (~2.0 deg at the recommended point) + settle (550 ms) + max per-tick pose-target step (2.13 deg) pinned TOGETHER at one (omega, zeta, art, arm, slew) point - never the hold pose alone; (b) zero-straight-line yaw as an EXACT identity (1e-9, measured 0.000000000); (c) AC-087 floor re-pinned on the DETERMINISTIC unit proxy (browser-proxy spread 0.0494/0.0603/0.3599 rad is noise, not a floor anchor); (d) AC-088 re-scoped to the fragment-stage `uTireGradient*` uniform seam (the VBO vertex-colour measurement is blind BY CONSTRUCTION: upperAvg==lowerAvg==0.28565); (e) envelope re-derived from the measured peak (0.2295 rad) or the pose held inside 0.2250 (the recommended variant does the latter); (f) the 3-frame drift-gate regression guard; (g) the GAIN_eff=+1.0 forbidden-null contract is SUPERSEDED by the full model (gain stays 0.5; the V-null knowledge is retained for the record).
8. **RISKS Phase B must address:** GF-15 steer chatter (22.6 deg far-side swing at 4 Hz square-wave steer - a property of the LATCH design, needs a mitigation decision); canopy mismatch (glass.pass.ts:1048,1086 never reads driftYawOffsetRad - a bigger slide amplifies it); collision.utils.ts:410,417-418 must reset the pose state on bounce; computeDriftYawOffset dead export (drift.model.ts:363) wired or deleted in the same step (the natural home for the pose state); the spring steps on the 60 Hz physics tick, NEVER the render path (a per-frame spring would be display-rate dependent: 2.4x faster at 144 Hz).
9. **FILE SET:** drift.model.ts (model + constants + pose-state types), physics.step.service.ts (tick wiring + state carry), collision.utils.ts (pose reset), car.pass.ts (uniform feed), glass.pass.ts (canopy decision), drift.model.test.ts + physics.step.service.test.ts + car.pass.test.ts (RED homes), docs/browser-tests/scenarios/p1-turn-drift-green-smoke.html (smoke checks). Phase B decides the final packet shape.

### Why this mix wins on the criterion (fun / exciting)

The verdict asked for the exciting arcade feeling with a much sharper bounce-back. Only the full mix delivers all three measurable exciters: (1) a 5x bigger, BOUNDED hold slide (proxy 0.0494 -> 0.2266 rad = the slide READS as a drift); (2) a countersteer that CATCHES in 0.30 s (was mirrored inversion) with a 2.2 deg far-side pop + decaying ring (the snap-back); (3) a 0.10/0.20 s entry attack (was 0.25/0.75 s - the commitment). Track A alone would put a cosmetic pop on a car still sliding the wrong way - incoherent, not fun. The game-feel measurements confirm the pop is real, speed-independent, and coherent under partial countersteer (GF-16).

- `decision`: '**A BIGGER SLIDE** - the PHYSICAL half of the feel. The countersteer CATCH (the crisper-recovery half) is delivered by the model itself, not by a competing visual lever.'
- `why`: 'The PHASE-A merge already established that the root cause is PHYSICAL: the countersteer MIRRORS the slide (the centrifugal push is yaw-rate-driven, so a countersteer REVERSES it, and the gate `steer * sign(slip) > 0` closes at the zero-slip crossing; authority 3.4 vs push 8.4 m/s^2), so a purely visual transient gain would put a cosmetic pop on a car still sliding the wrong way. - `named_lever`: '`NEATRACING_DRIFT_MIN_SLIDE_PROXY_RAD` (the NAMED floor) over the DETERMINISTIC unit proxy `computeDriftSlideProxyRad(slipAngleRad) = |slip| * |GAIN - 1|` (recommended 0.20 rad), plus the coupled constraint `NEATRACING_DRIFT_MAX_SLIP_ANGLE_RAD >= 0.40` at `GAIN = 0.5` that makes the floor reachable.'
- `not_invented`: 'The 2026-10-24 user verdict accepted the MECHANICS and did NOT name the direction. D-11 is the explicit decision the packet required, and it is recorded HERE - in the plan, BEFORE any production edit - so the RED slice pins a DECIDED direction instead of inventing one.'

### The ENVELOPE re-derivation (the two-contract decision)

- `declared_pose_envelope`: '**0.3050 rad** = `MAX_SLIP (0.45) * GAIN (0.5) + POSE_STEER_YAW_RAD (0.08)`. This is the STATIC worst case: the slip term at the full opposite steer PLUS the articulation term at the full opposite steer, which is exactly the case the orchestrator directed (slip x gain + |ARTICULATION| at full opposite steer). It is a LIMIT, not a clamp - the pose is never clamped.'
- `tuning_target`: '**0.2250 rad** - the RED slice MEASURES the peak |pose| on SCN-DRIFT-01 and pins it against this tighter target (the recommended variant measures 0.2246 rad, 0.19 % inside). The rationale: the two envelope terms are ANTI-CORRELATED in time - the committed slip unwinds at EXIT_RATE 2.0 rad/s while the articulation slews at SLEW 20/s (0.1 s) - so the reachable |poseTarget| peaks near 0.205 rad, not at the static sum. This keeps omega = 18 load-bearing for the tuning target.'
- `fallback`: 'A measured peak above 0.2250 rad but at most 0.3050 rad re-records the ceiling with the MEASURED value in BOTH pins - the LIMIT DOES NOT MOVE. A measured peak above 0.3050 rad means the MODEL is at fault: BLOCK and escalate via 00.cross-tier-helper. The limit is NEVER widened.'
- `why_not_0.2250_as_the_limit`: 'The 0.2250 rad figure bounds the SLIP TERM ONLY. The articulation term can add 0.08 rad in the same direction during a countersteer, so a pose bound of 0.2250 rad would FAIL a correct implementation - the fixture-gate probe itself measures 0.2658 rad for a correct build.'

The +-pi heading crossing MUST use a shortest-path signed delta (house idiom wrapSignedAngle, ai.autopilot.ts:64) or the camera spins 2pi. NO slew limit in this slice (a first-order filter does not reduce the release RATE; a tight slew limit would re-create a stuck offset during sustained corner drifts; the release is already physically bounded at 2.5 rad/s). A >= 3-4 rad/s slew is a LATER option if the whip is still objectionable."
    CD4_starfield: "cameraPose.yawRadians RE-SOURCED to carSceneYawRad(aim) (today it copies the car BODY yaw L1000 <- carPoseBag.yawRad) - the sky is at infinity: a starfield locked to the body heading would SLIDE RELATIVE TO THE WORLD by the slip angle during every drift once the camera swings with the aim. LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic. The pi/2 scene offset is RETAINED (c1). The pitch value is NOT touched here (CD6)."
    CD5_latch: "RATIFIED AGAIN - no release path (a release re-baselines the closed GAP-N4: the D1.3 deficit 25.62 km/h, the c-band [0.504, 0.626], the 0.2250 pose envelope, G-1..G-7) => outside the SLIM mandate. The 2nd rejection names the CAMERA first, and the latch is PRECISELY what makes the camera defect load-bearing (a constant slip => a constant camera offset) => the camera fix is the CORRECT+SUFFICIENT response to this rejection. PRE-REGISTERED ESCALATION: a THIRD user rejection after the camera slice lands => the latch re-decision re-opens at PLAN level with a full re-baseline - never inside a loop-back."
    CD6_horizon: "the horizon defect is REAL but OUT OF SCOPE - the true down-pitch is atan2(HEIGHT/2, BACK+LOOKAHEAD) = atan2(1.2, 13.5) = 0.0885 rad; the constant is 0.12 (L525) => the horizon NDC is tan(0.12)/tan(30 deg) = +0.2089 vs the true +0.1532 => a ~0.055 NDC (~20 px @720p) band, and the code comment 'the starfield tile ends exactly at the geometric horizon' is FALSE by 0.0315 rad. This slice does NOT change camera geometry (eye/target heights+distances unchanged) => independent of CD1 => routed to Step 14H (Starfield polish, [PLANNED]). SIGN TRAP for 14H: the constant is DOWN-positive (starfield.pass.ts:105-106 'positive pitches the camera down'); substituting the look-up-positive -0.0885 FLIPS THE SKY BELOW THE HORIZON; 14H must re-derive BOTH the pitch and the horizon NDC from the geometry and RED-contract u_horizonNdcY in (0, 1)."
    CD7_crab_gain: "FLAGGED, NOT BUNDLED - the rendered crab is 12.9 deg vs the physical slip 25.5 deg. Raising the visual gain re-baselines the 0.2250 envelope (a physics-contract change) => a separate wave. After CD1 the body 12.9 deg crab becomes the visible slide cue against a STRAIGHT road (the intended read); if the user wants more, this is the next candidate."
  learning_event_draft: "for W5 capture (07-logging), category workflow-gap / unverified-premise: a user-reported camera symptom was routed to an unverified mechanism - the plan camera premise was ASSERTED, never read against the live code; the D-MEMO exonerated the camera for 'stuck' without explaining the residual 'awkward' symptom; the SAME gap recurred on the 2nd user gate. Prevention: before exonerating a subsystem, READ its live code and record the EXACT mechanism; a residual symptom must be EXPLAINED, not DEFERRED."

    dead_premise: "The original W4b premise read the camera aim from the pose bag (carPoseBag.driftYawOffsetRadRad = car.drift.pose.pose, browser-entry.ts:972) and treated cameraPose.yawRadians as the camera aim channel. BOTH ARE DEAD. The pose is the BODY yaw source (the pose spring at physics.step.service.ts:454-459), and cameraPose is a STARFIELD-ONLY channel (the star layer yaw at browser-entry.ts:1000) - the real camera is the pair lookAtInto(view, cameraWorld, target) + perspectiveInto (browser-entry.ts:622 and :593) and its aim comes from the CAR NOSE. The 2026-10-27 audits measured the consequence: the camera is a PURE STATELESS function of the nose, so the published 0.4502 rad (25.85 deg) slide produces ZERO screen-space translation of the 24.06 deg off-axis travel, and the body shows only 33.8 percent of the slide (the G-M3 defect). The 43 fixture checks and the A1-A11 contracts can ALL pass with a FROZEN camera, so the W4b contract set as written could not have caught the defect it was written to fix."
    rewrite_1_one_aim_law: "ONE aim law, ONE function, THREE call sites. The camera aim is computed ONCE per frame by a single named function and read by the camera placement + the look target (browser-entry.ts:935-940 and :1010-1012) AND by the starfield yaw (:1000). The original packet had the unfiltered aim at :935-937 and :1010-1012 but the FILTERED offset only at :1000 (the F4 inconsistency) - the two consumers could therefore never agree, and the starfield slides relative to the world during a drift."
    rewrite_2_the_aim_source: "The aim is sourced from the TRAVEL HEADING PUBLISHED ON THE PHYSICS STATE (the named field travelHeadingRad = heading + published slip, wrapped), NOT from a local re-derivation and NOT from the pose bag. The audits are explicit (R-M1): the travel direction on the state and the camera change land in the SAME slice, because a camera fixed while the state cannot say which way the car is going is the exact defect the wave exists to remove. The velocityHeading the physics service already computes at physics.step.service.ts:462 and DISCARDS at :475 (the G-M1 break line) becomes the published field."
    rewrite_3_the_body_shares_the_slice: "The BODY yaw is switched to the PUBLISHED slip in the SAME slice (the pose spring call site at physics.step.service.ts:457 passes the committed slip today). The camera and the body therefore land together, so the frame can never be internally inconsistent (a travel-locked camera with a crabbing body is forbidden)."
    rewrite_4_the_rate_law: "The follow rate is PROPORTIONAL, not a fixed time constant: the per-tick aim change scales with the SPEED times the shared drift amount (the user law S-1/S-4). The CONTESTED constants NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_FOLLOW_TAU_S = 0.08 (a fixed tau) and NEATRACING_CHASE_CAMERA_TRAVEL_AIM_GAIN = 1 (a fixed gain) are RETIRED and REPLACED by S-1/S-4-conformant NAMED exports with a derived JSDoc.   status: '[DONE] - 2026-10-28 by the 04-implementing instance: the NEW module examples/neatRacing/track/track.racing-line.ts is CREATED and exports the PINNED API VERBATIM (TrackRacingLinePoint { offsetM, curvaturePerM, targetSpeedUnitsPerS } and buildTrackRacingLine(samples)), so ALL EIGHT racing-line contracts (RL-1..RL-8) are GREEN - ONE point per sample in the sample order, the offset EXACTLY ZERO on the straights, the apex-biased offset pointing INSIDE the corner, the reversed traversal flipping the apex sign, the offset CLAMPED to the drivable half-width at every sample, the layout invariance, the BIT-EXACT rotation invariance (the delta is EXACTLY 0, not 1e-9) and the published curvature speed profile. The DECIDED magnitudes (the 200 m straight corner radius, the 0.005 1/m straight curvature threshold, the DERIVED 39.605 m/s^2 lateral limit, the 16 m^2 apex-bias gain and the 3-sample curvature-window radius), the MEASURED bands (the 1.920 m apex offset at R = 8 m, the 0.187 m at R = 60 m and the 0.057 m on the real demo track) and the implementation notes are RECORDED in this plan (Latest validation evidence + this plan-tail PlanUpdate). NO autopilot file was edited (the consumer seam belongs to the sibling slice P1-ai-centerline) and ONLY this slice status was flipped.'
  mandate: 'implement AC-082 exactly as the Step 14M slice packet defines it (the NEW deterministic curvature-derived racing-line module, apex-biased, exactly zero on straights, clamped to the drivable half-width, seed-invariant for a fixed layout, derived from the existing spline samples), make the RED contracts RL-1..RL-8 green, record the decided magnitudes and the implementation notes in-plan, flip ONLY this slice status and run the slice-advancement + plan-sync gates on the final bytes - code-level Jest ONLY (NO browser, NO Chrome DevTools MCP, NO CDP - the user mandate), NO child agent, git READ-ONLY'
  files_changed:
    - 'examples/neatRacing/track/track.racing-line.ts (NEW - the AC-082 racing-line module: the PINNED TrackRacingLinePoint interface, buildTrackRacingLine and the FIVE named constants)'
    - 'plans/neatracing-voxel-racer.plans.md (the slice status marker, the Latest validation evidence entry and this record)'
  file_cap: '1 new production file + THIS plan - UNDER the 3-file cap (the slice lists the module, the RED test file and this plan). NO *.utils.ts helper file was created, because the cap leaves no room for one and the module needs no helper. The RED test file was NOT edited - the contracts were made to PASS, never rewritten. The temporary measurement harness lived OUTSIDE the repo (the OS temp directory), so the tracked tree carries NO artifact of it.'
  decided_magnitudes:
    straight_corner_radius: 'NEATRACING_RACING_LINE_STRAIGHT_CORNER_RADIUS_M = 200 (m) - the flattest corner the line still treats as a corner. Its reciprocal threshold NEATRACING_RACING_LINE_STRAIGHT_CURVATURE_PER_M = 0.005 (1/m) is the straight dead-band: at or below it the offset is EXACTLY 0 and the target speed is the top speed.'
    lateral_acceleration_limit: 'NEATRACING_RACING_LINE_LATERAL_ACCELERATION_LIMIT_M_PER_S2 = 89^2 / 200 = 39.605 (m/s^2) - DERIVED from the reused NEATRACING_PHYSICS_MAX_SPEED_UNITS_PER_S = 89, NOT tuned, so the flattest corner the line reacts to is exactly drivable AT the top speed and the speed profile has NO step at the straight/corner boundary. NO existing named lateral-grip constant exists in the physics layer to import (the drift model owns only the 2 m/s^2 momentum hold, the 0.2 rad grip falloff and the slip limits), so the racing line owns its own derived limit and imports ONLY the top speed - with NO import cycle (physics/* never imports examples/neatRacing/track/*).'
    apex_bias_gain: 'NEATRACING_RACING_LINE_APEX_BIAS_GAIN_M2 = 16 (m^2) - the offset per unit of EXCESS curvature. Calibrated so the tight R = 8 m fixture takes a 1.920 m apex offset (inside the 6 m drivable half-width and inside the 3 m AC-085 bound) while the R = 60 m lap fixture takes 0.1867 m and the real demo track 0.0573 m.'
    curvature_window_radius: 'NEATRACING_RACING_LINE_CURVATURE_WINDOW_RADIUS_SAMPLES = 3 (samples) - a SYMMETRIC circular 7-sample moving average over the closed ring. Deliberately small: a wider window would bleed the corner curvature back onto the straight and break the straight-zero clause (the AI-4 handoff probe at index 32 still reads a curvature of EXACTLY 0).'
    laws: 'the offset = clamp(16 x sign(k) x max(0, |k| - 0.005), -width/2, +width/2) with width/2 the SAME drivable half-width the Step 14I containment uses (physics/collision.utils.ts); the target speed = |k| <= 0.005 ? 89 : min(89, sqrt(39.605 / |k|)). The SIGN is POSITIVE to the LEFT of travel (the repo left-normal convention - SplineSample.innerOffsetWorld) and the curvature is POSITIVE when turning LEFT.'
  measured_bands:
    red_fixture: 'the RED R = 8 m stadium (24 arc samples, 128 samples, a 12 m road): apex offset +1.920 m, apex curvature 0.125 1/m, apex target 17.80 m/s, EVERY straight offset EXACTLY 0, max |offset| 1.920 m, the reversed apex -1.920 m, the rotation delta EXACTLY 0.'
    autopilot_tight_fixture: 'R = 8 m, 25 arc samples, 130 samples: apex +1.920 m; the worst straight-region offset 0.6347 m at index 39 (the corner-ENTRY ramp - the 3-sample window bleeds 3 samples past the entry, which is EXPECTED and is NOT a straight sample); the AI-4 handoff probe at index 32 reads offset 0 / curvature 0 / target EXACTLY 89; the AI-5 probe at index 46 reads target 17.80 m/s.'
    autopilot_lap_fixture: 'R = 60 m, 496 samples: apex offset +0.1867 m, apex curvature 0.01667 1/m, apex target 48.75 m/s, every straight offset EXACTLY 0, the reversed apex -0.1867 m, the rotation delta EXACTLY 0.'
    real_demo_track: 'generateTrack(NEATRACING_DEMO_TRACK_GENERATION), seed 42, layoutVersion 1, sizeBucket large, 144 samples, road widths 27.8-32.2 m: max |offset| 0.0573 m, max |curvature| 0.00858 1/m (R ~ 116 m), the target speed spans 67.93 .. 89 m/s, 107 of 144 samples publish an EXACTLY zero offset, the rotation delta EXACTLY 0.'
  implementation_notes:
    geometry: 'the SIGNED Menger curvature k = 2 x cross(b-a, c-a) / (|b-a| x |b-c| x |a-c|) over the three-sample window of the CLOSED ring, POSITIVE when the loop turns LEFT, smoothed into the SINGLE published curvaturePerM profile. The offset AND the speed are both derived from that ONE profile, so the table carries no second geometry (AC-086).'
    bit_exact_rotation: 'the three side lengths are computed as sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy) and NOT with Math.hypot, because the explicit form is BIT-IDENTICAL when a rigid rotation negates and swaps the coordinate differences (IEEE-754 addition and multiplication are commutative). The rotation invariance is therefore EXACT (delta EXACTLY 0, not 1e-9) and the reversed traversal flips the sign EXACTLY.'
    deviation_apex_biased: 'the step-level AC-082 parenthetical "inside on corner entry, outside on exit" is implemented as an APEX-BIASED profile - the offset rises from 0 at the corner entry to the apex peak and falls back to 0 at the exit (INSIDE through the corner, back on the centerline after it). The classic out-in-out line (a NEGATIVE offset on entry and exit) is DELIBERATELY NOT built: the RED slice decided that only the apex MIDPOINT points INSIDE is pinned (NO magnitude, NO entry/exit profile asserted), the AC-082 ledger row carries only the apex-inside clause, and a negative exit offset would fight the AC-085 3 m bound and the zero-on-straights clause. This is the ONE documented deviation and it is compatible with every pinned contract.'
    straight_zero_is_geometric: 'the 200 m dead-band makes "EXACTLY ZERO on straights" a property of a REAL layout (a generated track-s nominal straight is a sampled curve with a small non-zero curvature), not a fixture artifact.'
    allocation: 'the table is built ONCE per layout and the per-frame AI path reads the published table and allocates NO TABLE (SCOPED 2026-10-29, FP-14M-08: the ORIGINAL "allocates NOTHING" claim was true of the TABLE only - the per-frame step still builds its own small step-input object and rescans the sample list). The module allocates two Float64Arrays plus the point array per BUILD, never per frame.'
    purity: 'a PURE function of the frozen sample list - NO RNG, NO clock, NO Date.now, NO Math.random, NO shared module state - so two builds of the same layout are identical and the line is SEED-INVARIANT (the layout seed never enters the module at all). ES2023, named constants, JSDoc on every export, no any.'
  acs_satisfied:

ALL EIGHT racing-line contracts (RL-1..RL-8) are GREEN by name.'
    - 'AC-086 (the track-relative surface): the module publishes the SIGNED curvature profile and the curvature-derived target speed alongside the offset, from ONE profile, so the Phase 2 consumers read ONE track-relative surface and NOT a second source of truth. The rotation invariance is EXACT (delta EXACTLY 0). The autopilot-side EXPOSURE of that surface to the Phase 2 consumers belongs to the sibling slice P1-ai-centerline.'

If the next slice instead steers TOWARD the racing line, the target becomes the line itself (0.1867 m at R = 60 m, 1.920 m at R = 8 m) - still inside 3 m, but by only 1.08 m.'
    - 'THE R = 8 m FIXTURE CORNER IS NOT DRIVABLE AT ANY SPEED BY THIS MODEL: the AI minimum turn radius is 89 / (2 x 1) = 44.5 m (the EXPRESSION is CORRECTED 2026-10-29, FP-14M-06: it read 89 / (2 x 2) = 22.25 m, which was wrong - the full steer axis is 1, not 2 - and the RESULT 44.5 m and the model-limit reading are right), speed-independent, so the published 17.80 m/s there is a PROFILE value that discriminates the INPUT lanes (AI-4 / AI-5) and NOT a drivable corner. The drivable judgement belongs to the R = 60 m lap fixture, whose published target 48.75 m/s needs steer 0.742 (inside the unit cap) and 39.6 m/s^2 of lateral acceleration, which is INSIDE the RED-measured reachable envelope of 59.44 m/s^2 at steer 0.6.'
    - 'THE STRAIGHT-ZERO DEPENDS ON THE 200 m THRESHOLD: a layout whose nominal straight is tighter than R = 200 m would publish a NON-ZERO offset there.   implementation:
    live_symmetry: 'createEditorLiveSymmetry ({toggle, base}) is the LIVE mirror-X surface: the tool frame symmetry policy freezes its axis flags at construction, so a mid-session toggle flip could never reach the paint path. The wrapper reads toggle.checked AT PAINT TIME, builds the two frozen policies ONCE from the base mirror-Y / mirror-Z flags (so the emitted target list stays exactly deterministic) and resolves the matching policy per paint. The edit loop now consumes this live surface instead of the frozen base policy. The toggle itself is pre-checked to the default, so mirror-X is ON from the first paint (NEATRACING_EDITOR_DEFAULT_MIRROR_X).'
    live_save: 'createEditorLiveSave ({modelName, readSource, fetchImpl, mirrorXEnabled}) owns the immediate save. The flight: resolve the model name (no model -> skipped-no-model) -> resolve the fetch seam (no seam -> skipped-no-seam; both statuses are SILENT, because a missing dev server is not a failure) -> project the working volume into a section 7.2 document -> measure the body -> refuse an over-budget payload BEFORE any request leaves the editor -> PUT /api/models/:name with the application/json content type -> POST /api/models/:name/rebuild to trigger the RebuildCoordinator flight (the envelope code dev-server/rebuild-coalesced maps to coalesced, anything else to started). The flight is LATEST-WINS: the saves enqueued while a request is in flight collapse into ONE follow-up request carrying the CURRENT volume, so one edit burst is one save. The save never rejects - every path resolves into a labeled result.'
    storage_form: 'The half-width symmetric form is used ONLY when the mirror-X toggle is ON and the volume is VERIFIED mirror-symmetric (isEditorVolumeMirrorSymmetric - every row must mirror onto itself across the x axis). Then the stored document keeps the LEFT 64 columns with meta.symmetric true and the loader mirrors the stored col c onto dims[0]-1-c; every other volume keeps the FULL 128 columns with meta.symmetric false, so the right half can never be silently dropped. The document palette is index-aligned with the editor palette ([EMPTY, ...entries.slice(1)]), the rows are the section 7.2 RLE hex pairs (<runLen:2hex><paletteIdx:2hex>, a 255-cell run cap), out-of-range palette indices clamp to 0 and meta.dims is [128, 128, 128].'
    boot: 'editor-entry.ts boot step 5c creates the live symmetry over toolframe.controls.symmetryToggle and the live save over the model name, the working volume, the palette and the toggle state. The live save drives a SEPARATE deps.saveFetch seam (the tool frame GET-only deps.fetch seam stays untouched, so the PINNED editor-entry.test.ts assertions keep working). The rebuild executor calls liveSave.enqueueSave() on FULL rebuilds only, right after publishWorkingVolume(). The pointer edit loop receives symmetry: liveSymmetry. The session exposes session.liveSave and stop() calls liveSave.stop().'
  deviations:
    - 'THE SAVE RIDES THE FULL-REBUILD FLIGHT, NOT THE POINTER EVENT: the executor enqueues the save only for request.mode === full, after publishWorkingVolume(). The dirty AABB +- 1 window only remeshes the edited slices, so saving from it would storm the model store with one PUT per slice window; the full flight collapses an edit burst into exactly one save. The AC-021 "every edit enqueues the immediate save" clause is therefore satisfied at the EDIT-FLIGHT granularity (one flight per edit burst), which the owner suite pins.'
    - 'THE STORAGE FORM IS SYMMETRIC ONLY WHEN VERIFIED: the half-width form requires the mirror-X toggle ON and a VERIFIED symmetric volume. Storing an unverified volume in the half-width form would silently drop the right half (the loader mirrors the stored half back onto the full width), so the verification is the safety interlock. Every other volume keeps the full width with meta.symmetric false.'
    - 'THE MIRROR-X FLAGS ARE READ AT PAINT TIME THROUGH A WRAPPER, NOT BY EDITING editor.symmetry.ts: the pure symmetry module freezes its flags at construction and its file is OUT of files_to_change, so the live surface is a wrapper that selects between two pre-built frozen policies per paint.'
    - 'THE BODY BUDGET IS MIRRORED, NOT IMPORTED: the editor constant NEATRACING_EDITOR_MAX_SAVE_BODY_BYTES (8 MiB) mirrors the server NEATRACING_MAX_SAVE_BODY_BYTES, because the server module cannot be imported into the browser bundle. The parity is PINNED by a test that imports the server constant, so a drift on either side breaks the lane.'
    - 'THE BODY IS MEASURED IN BYTES BY CONSTRUCTION: the payload is ASCII (the model name matches the store name pattern, the palette holds byte values, the rows are hex), so the string length IS the UTF-8 byte length - TextEncoder is absent in the jest jsdom env.'

```yaml
fix_packet:
  id: fix-packet-P1-outer-edge-geometry-iteration-1
  slice_id: P1-outer-edge-geometry
  iteration: 1
  status: REQUEST_CHANGES
  goal: address-requested-changes
  trigger: specialist-review
  source: 'the FULL-severity pre-green specialist review of the NEW seam module examples/neatRacing/track/track.edge.ts - the api-contract-reviewer (Tier 3), dispatched by the review-coordinator (Tier 2) on a validated Tier-2 dispatch packet. The verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES with TWO MAJOR contract defects and TWO MINOR doc defects. The reviewer confirmed the IMPLEMENTATION substance (the MEASURED 1.0 m drift space, the >= 90 degree saturation, the CCW -> outerSideSign -1 convention, the worldZ = -generatorY mirroring confirmed against track.slabs.ts / road-edge.ts / collision.utils.ts, the byte-identical nearest-chord rule, the purity and the determinism) - ONLY the PUBLISHED CONTRACT is at fault.'
  files_to_change:
    - examples/neatRacing/track/track.edge.ts
  findings:
    - id: FP-14U-01
      severity: MAJOR
      anchor: 'examples/neatRacing/track/track.edge.ts:63-72 (the module header) vs :286-292 (resolveTrackEdgeProfile) and :762-780 (buildSplineEdge)'
      defect: 'the header publishes a continuity invariant the code does not deliver - THE WIDTH FUNCTION ITSELF IS CONTINUOUS ... the published per-chord measure is that function''s sample at the chord''s MIDPOINT ... the chord band and the sampled ribbon band agree EXACTLY and no reader can measure a different edge from another reader. The implementation is PIECEWISE CONSTANT per chord (buildChordEdge publishes the chord''s own mean of the two vertex turn magnitudes, with no interpolation along the chord) and the spline publication (buildSplineEdge) reuses the OWNING CHORD''s midpoint measure while carrying the SAMPLE''s own interpolated width - so the two publications do NOT agree exactly and the file contradicts itself at :286-292.'
      decision: 'THE ORCHESTRATOR DECIDES (the reviewer offered two fixes): the IMPLEMENTATION is fixed, not only the prose. The per-spline-sample publication publishes the LOCAL corner measure - the ONE continuous corner-measure function of the loop position, sampled AT the sample - so the width profile the seam publishes is CONTINUOUS at the sample granularity and the two granularities become provable samples of the SAME function. The per-chord publication keeps its value BYTE-IDENTICAL (its measure IS the midpoint sample of that same function), so the three RED contracts are untouched. The prose is then reconciled to state EXACTLY what is true.'
      required_change:
